This may be accomplished exactly as has been done above for energy, but with a little bit more care, because the matrices elements of the coordinate and momentum operators, in the Fock state basis, are not diagonal:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\langle x\rangle(0) & =\frac{1}{2}(\langle 31|+\langle 32|) \hat{x}(|31\rangle+|32\rangle) \\
& =\frac{1}{2}(\langle 31| \hat{x}|32\rangle+\langle 32| \hat{x}|31\rangle) \\
& =\frac{1}{2} \frac{x_{0}}{\sqrt{2}}(\sqrt{32}+\sqrt{32})=4 x_{0} \\
\langle p\rangle(0) & =\frac{1}{2}(\langle 31|+\langle 32|) \hat{p}(|31\rangle+|32\rangle) \\
& =\frac{1}{2}(\langle 31| \hat{p}|32\rangle+\langle 32| \hat{p}|31\rangle) \\
& =\frac{1}{2} \frac{m \omega_{0} x_{0}}{\sqrt{2}}(\sqrt{32}-\sqrt{32})=0
\end{aligned}
$$

Plugging these expressions into Eq. (**), we get

$$
\langle x\rangle=4 x_{0} \cos \omega_{0} t, \quad\langle p\rangle=-4 m \omega_{0} x_{0} \sin \omega_{0} t
$$

Note that the exact answer could be different if there was a phase shift between the component Fock states. However, even in this case the expectation values of the coordinate and momentum would oscillate with the oscillator's frequency $\omega_{0}$.

question:
对于一维谐振子，计算：
(i) 能量的期望值，以及
(ii) 坐标和动量的期望值的时间演化，假设在初始时刻 $(t=0)$，其处于以下态矢描述的状态：

$$
|\alpha\rangle=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(|31\rangle+|32\rangle)
$$

其中 $|n\rangle$ 是振子的定态（Fock）态的态矢。
solution:
(i) 在这个哈密顿系统中，总能量是守恒的，因此我们可以在初始时刻计算它：

$$
\langle E\rangle=\langle\alpha(0)| \hat{H}|\alpha(0)\rangle=\frac{1}{2}(\langle 31|+\langle 32|) \hat{H}(|31\rangle+|32\rangle)
$$

利用哈密顿量在费克态 $n$ 的基底中是对角的这一事实，其对角元素等于 $E_{n}=\hbar \omega_{0}(n+1 / 2)$，我们得到

$$
\langle E\rangle=\frac{1}{2}(\langle 31| \hat{H}|31\rangle+\langle 32| \hat{H}|32\rangle)=\frac{\hbar \omega_{0}}{2}\left[\left(31+\frac{1}{2}\right)+\left(32+\frac{1}{2}\right)\right]=32 \hbar \omega_{0}
$$

(ii) $x$ 和 $p$ 的期望值的时间演化可以从讲义的公式 (5.36) 中获得，其中 $U=m \omega_{0}^{2} x^{2} / 2$：

$$
\langle\dot{x}\rangle=\frac{\langle p\rangle}{m}, \quad\langle\dot{p}\rangle=-m \omega_{0}^{2}\langle x\rangle
$$

这些方程（与经典运动方程一致）具有众所周知的解

$$
\begin{aligned}
& \langle x\rangle(t)=\langle x\rangle(0) \cos \omega_{0} t+\frac{\langle p\rangle(0)}{m \omega_{0}} \sin \omega_{0} t \\
& \langle p\rangle(t)=\langle p\rangle(0) \cos \omega_{0} t-m \omega_{0}\langle x\rangle(0) \sin \omega_{0} t
\end{aligned}
$$

所以现在唯一需要做的就是找到这些可观测量在 $t=0$ 时的期望值。这可以完全按照上面对能量的计算方法进行，但需要更加小心，因为坐标和动量算符在费克态基底中的矩阵元素不是对角的：

$$
\begin{aligned}
\langle x\rangle(0) & =\frac{1}{2}(\langle 31|+\langle 32|) \hat{x}(|31\rangle+|32\rangle) \\
& =\frac{1}{2}(\langle 31| \hat{x}|32\rangle+\langle 32| \hat{x}|31\rangle) \\
& =\frac{1}{2} \frac{x_{0}}{\sqrt{2}}(\sqrt{32}+\sqrt{32})=4 x_{0} \\
\langle p\rangle(0) & =\frac{1}{2}(\langle 31|+\langle 32|) \hat{p}(|31\rangle+|32\rangle) \\
& =\frac{1}{2}(\langle 31| \hat{p}|32\rangle+\langle 32| \hat{p}|31\rangle) \\
& =\frac{1}{2} \frac{m \omega_{0} x_{0}}{\sqrt{2}}(\sqrt{32}-\sqrt{32})=0
\end{aligned}
$$

将这些表达式代入方程 (**) 中，我们得到

$$
\langle x\rangle=4 x_{0} \cos \omega_{0} t, \quad\langle p\rangle=-4 m \omega_{0} x_{0} \sin \omega_{0} t
$$

注意，如果组成费克态之间存在相移，精确答案可能会不同。然而，即便在这种情况下，坐标和动量的期望值也会以振荡器的频率 $\omega_{0}$ 振荡。

question: Simplify the following double commutator: $\left[\hat{r}_{j},\left[\hat{L}^{2}, \hat{r}_{j}\right]\right]$.
solution:
Solution: Using Eq. (5.150) of the lecture notes, we may write

$$
\begin{aligned}
\hat{A}_{\| \prime} & \equiv\left[\hat{r}_{j},\left[\hat{L}^{2}, \hat{r}_{j}\right]\right] \\
& \equiv\left[\hat{r}_{j},\left[\sum_{j^{\prime}=1}^{3} \hat{L}_{j^{\prime}}^{2}, \hat{r}_{j^{\prime}}\right]\right]=\sum_{j^{\prime}=1}^{3}\left[\hat{r}_{j},\left[\hat{L}_{j^{\prime}} \hat{L}_{j^{\prime}}, \hat{r}_{j^{\prime}}\right]\right]
\end{aligned}
$$

Let us start with spelling out the internal commutator in this expression. The calculations may be shortened a bit using the easily provable operator identity:

$$
[\hat{B} \hat{C}, \hat{D}]=\hat{B}[\hat{C}, \hat{D}]+[\hat{B}, \hat{D}] \hat{C}
$$

Indeed, taking $\hat{B}=\hat{C}=\hat{L}_{j^{\prime}}$ and $\hat{D}=\hat{r}_{j^{\prime}}$, we get

$$
\left[\hat{L}_{j^{\prime}} \hat{L}_{j^{\prime}}, \hat{r}_{j^{\prime}}\right]=\hat{L}_{j^{\prime}}\left[\hat{L}_{j^{\prime}}, \hat{r}_{j^{\prime}}\right]+\left[\hat{L}_{j^{\prime}}, \hat{r}_{j^{\prime}}\right] \hat{L}_{j^{\prime}}
$$

Applying Eq. (5.148) in the form,

$$
\left[\hat{L}_{j^{\prime}}, \hat{r}_{j^{\prime}}\right]=i \hbar \hat{r}_{j^{\prime}} \varepsilon_{j^{\prime} j^{\prime} j^{\prime \prime}}
$$

to both commutators on the right-hand side, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}
{\left[\hat{L}_{j^{\prime}} \hat{L}_{j^{\prime}}, \hat{r}_{j^{\prime}}\right] } & =\hat{L}_{j^{\prime}} i \hbar \hat{r}_{j^{\prime}} \varepsilon_{j^{\prime} j^{\prime} j^{\prime \prime}}+i \hbar \hat{r}_{j^{\prime \prime}} \varepsilon_{j^{\prime} j^{\prime} j^{\prime \prime}} \hat{L}_{j^{\prime \prime}} \\
& \equiv i \hbar \varepsilon_{j^{\prime} j^{\prime} j^{\prime \prime}}\left(\hat{L}_{j^{\prime}} \hat{r}_{j^{\prime \prime}}+\hat{r}_{j^{\prime \prime}} \hat{L}_{j^{\prime \prime}}\right)
\end{aligned}
$$

With this, the external commutator in Eq. (*) becomes $$
\begin{aligned}
{\left[\hat{r}_{j},\left[\hat{L}_{j^{\prime}} \hat{L}_{j^{\prime \prime}}, \hat{r}_{j^{\prime}}\right]\right] } & =i \hbar \varepsilon_{j^{\prime} j^{\prime} j^{\prime \prime}}\left(\left[\hat{r}_{j}, \hat{L}_{j^{\prime}} \hat{r}_{j^{\prime \prime}}\right]+\left[\hat{r}_{j}, \hat{r}_{j^{\prime \prime}} \hat{L}_{j^{\prime}}\right]\right) \\
& \equiv i \hbar \varepsilon_{j^{\prime} j^{\prime \prime} j^{\prime}}\left(\left[\hat{L}_{j^{\prime}} \hat{r}_{j^{\prime \prime}}, \hat{r}_{j}\right]+\left[\hat{r}_{j^{\prime \prime}} \hat{L}_{j^{\prime}}, \hat{r}_{j}\right]\right)
\end{aligned}
$$

(Note the swap of the indices $j^{\prime}$ and $j^{\prime \prime \prime}$ in the Levi-Civita symbol in the last expression, which compensates the sign reversal due to the swap of operands in both commutators.) Now we may apply the identity $\left({ }^{* *}\right)$ again to both commutators on the right-hand side: in the first case, with $\hat{B}=\hat{L}_{j^{\prime}}, \hat{C}=\hat{r}_{j^{\prime \prime}}$, and $\hat{D}=\hat{r}_{j}$, and in the second case, with $\hat{B}=\hat{r}_{j^{\prime \prime}}, \hat{C}=\hat{L}_{j^{\prime \prime}}$, and $\hat{D}=\hat{r}_{j}$. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
{\left[\hat{r}_{j},\left[\hat{L}_{j^{\prime}} \hat{L}_{j^{\prime \prime}}, \hat{r}_{j^{\prime}}\right]\right] } & =i \hbar \varepsilon_{j^{\prime} j^{\prime \prime} j^{\prime}}\left(\hat{L}_{j^{\prime}}\left[\hat{r}_{j^{\prime \prime}}, \hat{r}_{j}\right]+\left[\hat{L}_{j^{\prime \prime}}, \hat{r}_{j}\right] \hat{r}_{j^{\prime \prime}}+\hat{r}_{j^{\prime \prime}}\left[\hat{L}_{j^{\prime}}, \hat{r}_{j}\right]+\left[\hat{r}_{j^{\prime \prime}}, \hat{r}_{j}\right] \hat{L}_{j^{\prime}}\right) \\
& =i \hbar \varepsilon_{j^{\prime} j^{\prime \prime} j^{\prime}}\left(\left[\hat{L}_{j^{\prime}}, \hat{r}_{j}\right] \hat{r}_{j^{\prime \prime}}+\hat{r}_{j^{\prime \prime}}\left[\hat{L}_{j^{\prime}}, \hat{r}_{j}\right]\right)
\end{aligned}
$$

because the Cartesian coordinate operators commute regardless of their indices.
Let us apply to the commutator on the right-hand side of the last expression the basic Eq. $\left({ }^{* * *}\right)$ again, now in the form

$$
\left[\hat{L}_{j^{\prime}}, \hat{r}_{j}\right]=i \hbar \hat{r}_{j^{\prime \prime}} \varepsilon_{j^{\prime \prime} j^{\prime \prime}}
$$

where the index $j^{\prime \prime \prime}$ is complementary to the indices $j$ and $j^{\prime}$ (it does not necessarily coincide with either $j^{\prime}$ or $j^{\prime \prime \prime}$ ). The result is

$$
\begin{aligned}
{\left[\hat{r}_{j},\left[\hat{L}_{j^{\prime}} \hat{L}_{j^{\prime \prime}}, \hat{r}_{j^{\prime}}\right]\right] } & =i \hbar \varepsilon_{j^{\prime \prime} j^{\prime \prime} j^{\prime}}\left(i \hbar \hat{r}_{j^{\prime \prime}} \varepsilon_{j^{\prime \prime} j^{\prime \prime}} \hat{r}_{j^{\prime \prime}}+\hat{r}_{j^{\prime \prime}} i \hbar \hat{r}_{j^{\prime \prime}} \varepsilon_{j^{\prime \prime} j j^{\prime \prime}}\right) \\
& \equiv-2 \hbar^{2} \varepsilon_{j^{\prime \prime} j^{\prime \prime} j^{\prime}} \varepsilon_{j^{\prime \prime} j^{\prime \prime}} \hat{r}_{j^{\prime \prime}} \hat{r}_{j^{\prime \prime}}
\end{aligned}
$$

so that the operator in question is reduced to

$$
\hat{A}_{j j^{\prime}}=-2 \hbar^{2} \sum_{j^{\prime}=1}^{3} \varepsilon_{j^{\prime} j^{\prime \prime} j^{\prime}} \varepsilon_{j^{\prime \prime} j j^{\prime}} \hat{r}_{j} \hat{r}_{j^{\prime \prime}}
$$

Generally, the Levi-Civita product sums over a similar index may be calculated using the so-called 'contracted epsilon identity ${ }^{41}$, but in our case it is more prudent to use a more pedestrian way, because both indices $j^{\prime \prime \prime}$ and $j^{\prime \prime \prime \prime}$ depend on the summation index $j^{\prime \prime}$. Indeed, due to the index cycling symmetry, we need to consider not all nine possible combinations of the indices $j$ and $j^{\prime}$, but only three different cases-of which two may be analyzed in one shot (and give the same result).
(i) If $j^{\prime}=j$, then, by their definition, the indices $j^{\prime \prime \prime}$ and $j^{\prime \prime \prime \prime}$ are equal to each other for any $j^{\prime \prime}$, so that the Levi-Civita index product in sum $\left({ }^{* * * *}\right)$ equals $(-1)$ in both terms with $j^{\prime \prime} \neq j$. (In the term with $j^{\prime \prime}=j$, the product vanishes.) In the remaining two terms, the common index of the Cartesian coordinates takes both values not equal to $j$ (and hence to $j^{\prime}$ ), so that the result may be conveniently represented as

[^0]
[^0]:    ${ }^{41}$ See, e.g. Eq. (A.84b). 
 $$
\hat{A}_{j j}=2 \hbar^{2}\left(\hat{r}^{2}-\hat{r}_{j}^{2}\right)
$$

(ii) If $j=j^{\prime} \pm 1,{ }^{42}$ the sum in Eq. $\left({ }^{* * * *}\right)$ has not two, but just one nonvanishing term, because both the Levi-Civita symbols kill the terms with both $j^{\prime \prime}=j^{\prime}$ and $j^{\prime \prime}=j=j^{\prime} \pm$ 1. In the only remaining term of the sum, $j^{\prime \prime}=j^{\prime} \mp 1$, and hence, by its definition as the complementary one to $j^{\prime}$ and $j^{\prime \prime}$, the index $j^{\prime \prime \prime}$ is equal to $j^{\prime} \pm 1=j$, while the index $j^{\prime \prime \prime}$, by its definition as the complementary one to $j$ and $j^{\prime \prime}$, equals $j^{\prime}$. As the result, Eq. $\left({ }^{* * * *}\right)$ is reduced to

$$
\hat{A}_{j j^{\prime}}=-2 \hbar^{2} \varepsilon_{(j^{\prime} \mp 1)(j^{\prime} \pm 1) j^{\prime}} \varepsilon_{(j^{\prime} \mp 1)(j^{\prime} \pm 1) j^{\prime}} \hat{r}_{j} \hat{r}_{j^{\prime}}=-2 \hbar^{2} \hat{r}_{j} \hat{r}_{j^{\prime}}, \quad \text { for } j \neq j^{\prime}
$$

Both above results may be summarized as

$$
\hat{A}_{j j^{\prime}}=2 \hbar^{2}\left(\hat{r}^{2} \delta_{j j^{\prime}}-\hat{r}_{j} \hat{r}_{j^{\prime}}\right)
$$

The reader may have noticed an interesting analogy between this final result and the well-known classical expression for the contribution of an elementary mass $d m$ of a rigid body to its inertia tensor ${ }^{43}$ :

$$
d I_{j j^{\prime}}=d m\left(r^{2} \delta_{j j^{\prime}}-r_{j} r_{j^{\prime}}\right)
$$

question: 简化以下双重对易子：$\left[\hat{r}_{j},\left[\hat{L}^{2}, \hat{r}_{j}\right]\right]$。
solution:
解答：使用讲义中的方程 (5.150)，我们可以写为

$$
\begin{aligned}
\hat{A}_{\| \prime} & \equiv\left[\hat{r}_{j},\left[\hat{L}^{2}, \hat{r}_{j}\right]\right] \\
& \equiv\left[\hat{r}_{j},\left[\sum_{j^{\prime}=1}^{3} \hat{L}_{j^{\prime}}^{2}, \hat{r}_{j^{\prime}}\right]\right]=\sum_{j^{\prime}=1}^{3}\left[\hat{r}_{j},\left[\hat{L}_{j^{\prime}} \hat{L}_{j^{\prime}}, \hat{r}_{j^{\prime}}\right]\right]
\end{aligned}
$$

让我们从展开这个表达式中的内部对易子开始。计算可以通过使用易于证明的算符恒等式稍微简化：

$$
[\hat{B} \hat{C}, \hat{D}]=\hat{B}[\hat{C}, \hat{D}]+[\hat{B}, \hat{D}] \hat{C}
$$

确实，取 $\hat{B}=\hat{C}=\hat{L}_{j^{\prime}}$ 和 $\hat{D}=\hat{r}_{j^{\prime}}$，我们得到

$$
\left[\hat{L}_{j^{\prime}} \hat{L}_{j^{\prime}}, \hat{r}_{j^{\prime}}\right]=\hat{L}_{j^{\prime}}\left[\hat{L}_{j^{\prime}}, \hat{r}_{j^{\prime}}\right]+\left[\hat{L}_{j^{\prime}}, \hat{r}_{j^{\prime}}\right] \hat{L}_{j^{\prime}}
$$

应用方程 (5.148) 的形式，

$$
\left[\hat{L}_{j^{\prime}}, \hat{r}_{j^{\prime}}\right]=i \hbar \hat{r}_{j^{\prime}} \varepsilon_{j^{\prime} j^{\prime} j^{\prime \prime}}
$$

到右侧的两个对易子，我们得到

$$
\begin{aligned}
{\left[\hat{L}_{j^{\prime}} \hat{L}_{j^{\prime}}, \hat{r}_{j^{\prime}}\right] } & =\hat{L}_{j^{\prime}} i \hbar \hat{r}_{j^{\prime}} \varepsilon_{j^{\prime} j^{\prime} j^{\prime \prime}}+i \hbar \hat{r}_{j^{\prime \prime}} \varepsilon_{j^{\prime} j^{\prime} j^{\prime \prime}} \hat{L}_{j^{\prime \prime}} \\
& \equiv i \hbar \varepsilon_{j^{\prime} j^{\prime} j^{\prime \prime}}\left(\hat{L}_{j^{\prime}} \hat{r}_{j^{\prime \prime}}+\hat{r}_{j^{\prime \prime}} \hat{L}_{j^{\prime \prime}}\right)
\end{aligned}
$$

有了这个，方程 (*) 中的外部对易子变为

$$
\begin{aligned}
{\left[\hat{r}_{j},\left[\hat{L}_{j^{\prime}} \hat{L}_{j^{\prime \prime}}, \hat{r}_{j^{\prime}}\right]\right] } & =i \hbar \varepsilon_{j^{\prime} j^{\prime} j^{\prime \prime}}\left(\left[\hat{r}_{j}, \hat{L}_{j^{\prime}} \hat{r}_{j^{\prime \prime}}\right]+\left[\hat{r}_{j}, \hat{r}_{j^{\prime \prime}} \hat{L}_{j^{\prime}}\right]\right) \\
& \equiv i \hbar \varepsilon_{j^{\prime} j^{\prime \prime} j^{\prime}}\left(\left[\hat{L}_{j^{\prime}} \hat{r}_{j^{\prime \prime}}, \hat{r}_{j}\right]+\left[\hat{r}_{j^{\prime \prime}} \hat{L}_{j^{\prime}}, \hat{r}_{j}\right]\right)
\end{aligned}
$$

（注意最后表达式中 Levi-Civita 符号的指标 $j^{\prime}$ 和 $j^{\prime \prime \prime}$ 的交换，这补偿了由于在两个对易子中交换操作数而导致的符号反转。）现在我们可以再次将恒等式 $\left({ }^{* *}\right)$ 应用于右侧的两个对易子：在第一种情况下，取 $\hat{B}=\hat{L}_{j^{\prime}}, \hat{C}=\hat{r}_{j^{\prime \prime}}$，以及 $\hat{D}=\hat{r}_{j}$；在第二种情况下，取 $\hat{B}=\hat{r}_{j^{\prime \prime}}, \hat{C}=\hat{L}_{j^{\prime \prime}}$，以及 $\hat{D}=\hat{r}_{j}$。这得到

$$
\begin{aligned}
{\left[\hat{r}_{j},\left[\hat{L}_{j^{\prime}} \hat{L}_{j^{\prime \prime}}, \hat{r}_{j^{\prime}}\right]\right] } & =i \hbar \varepsilon_{j^{\prime} j^{\prime \prime} j^{\prime}}\left(\hat{L}_{j^{\prime}}\left[\hat{r}_{j^{\prime \prime}}, \hat{r}_{j}\right]+\left[\hat{L}_{j^{\prime \prime}}, \hat{r}_{j}\right] \hat{r}_{j^{\prime \prime}}+\hat{r}_{j^{\prime \prime}}\left[\hat{L}_{j^{\prime}}, \hat{r}_{j}\right]+\left[\hat{r}_{j^{\prime \prime}}, \hat{r}_{j}\right] \hat{L}_{j^{\prime}}\right) \\
& =i \hbar \varepsilon_{j^{\prime} j^{\prime \prime} j^{\prime}}\left(\left[\hat{L}_{j^{\prime}}, \hat{r}_{j}\right] \hat{r}_{j^{\prime \prime}}+\hat{r}_{j^{\prime \prime}}\left[\hat{L}_{j^{\prime}}, \hat{r}_{j}\right]\right)
\end{aligned}
$$

因为无论指标如何，笛卡尔坐标算符都是对易的。
让我们再次将基本方程 $\left({ }^{* * *}\right)$ 应用于最后表达式右侧的对易子，现在的形式为

$$
\left[\hat{L}_{j^{\prime}}, \hat{r}_{j}\right]=i \hbar \hat{r}_{j^{\prime \prime}} \varepsilon_{j^{\prime \prime} j^{\prime \prime}}
$$

其中指标 $j^{\prime \prime \prime}$ 是与指标 $j$ 和 $j^{\prime}$ 互补的（它不一定与 $j^{\prime}$ 或 $j^{\prime \prime \prime}$ 重合）。结果是

$$
\begin{aligned}
{\left[\hat{r}_{j},\left[\hat{L}_{j^{\prime}} \hat{L}_{j^{\prime \prime}}, \hat{r}_{j^{\prime}}\right]\right] } & =i \hbar \varepsilon_{j^{\prime \prime} j^{\prime \prime} j^{\prime}}\left(i \hbar \hat{r}_{j^{\prime \prime}} \varepsilon_{j^{\prime \prime} j^{\prime \prime}} \hat{r}_{j^{\prime \prime}}+\hat{r}_{j^{\prime \prime}} i \hbar \hat{r}_{j^{\prime \prime}} \varepsilon_{j^{\prime \prime} j j^{\prime \prime}}\right) \\
& \equiv-2 \hbar^{2} \varepsilon_{j^{\prime \prime} j^{\prime \prime} j^{\prime}} \varepsilon_{j^{\prime \prime} j^{\prime \prime}} \hat{r}_{j^{\prime \prime}} \hat{r}_{j^{\prime \prime}}
\end{aligned}
$$

因此，所讨论的算符简化为

$$
\hat{A}_{j j^{\prime}}=-2 \hbar^{2} \sum_{j^{\prime}=1}^{3} \varepsilon_{j^{\prime} j^{\prime \prime} j^{\prime}} \varepsilon_{j^{\prime \prime} j j^{\prime}} \hat{r}_{j} \hat{r}_{j^{\prime \prime}}
$$

一般来说，Levi-Civita 乘积在类似指标上的求和可以使用所谓的“收缩 epsilon 恒等式 ${ }^{41}$”来计算，但在我们的情况下，使用一种更简单的方法更为明智，因为两个指标 $j^{\prime \prime \prime}$ 和 $j^{\prime \prime \prime \prime}$ 依赖于求和指标 $j^{\prime \prime}$。确实，由于指标循环对称性，我们不需要考虑指标 $j$ 和 $j^{\prime}$ 的所有九种可能组合，而只需考虑三种不同情况，其中两种可以一次性分析（并给出相同结果）。
(i) 如果 $j^{\prime}=j$，那么根据它们的定义，任何 $j^{\prime \prime}$ 的指标 $j^{\prime \prime \prime}$ 和 $j^{\prime \prime \prime \prime}$ 相等，因此在求和中的 Levi-Civita 指标乘积在两个 $j^{\prime \prime} \neq j$ 的项中等于 $(-1)$。（在 $j^{\prime \prime}=j$ 的项中，乘积为零。）在剩余的两项中，笛卡尔坐标的公共指标取两个不等于 $j$（因此也不等于 $j^{\prime}$）的值，因此结果可以方便地表示为

[^0]
[^0]: ${ }^{41}$ 参见，例如，方程 (A.84b)。 
$$
\hat{A}_{j j}=2 \hbar^{2}\left(\hat{r}^{2}-\hat{r}_{j}^{2}\right)
$$

(ii) 如果 $j=j^{\prime} \pm 1,{ }^{42}$，方程 $\left({ }^{* * * *}\right)$ 中的求和不仅有两个，而是只有一个非零项，因为两个 Levi-Civita 符号消除了 $j^{\prime \prime}=j^{\prime}$ 和 $j^{\prime \prime}=j=j^{\prime} \pm 1$ 的项。在求和的唯一剩余项中，$j^{\prime \prime}=j^{\prime} \mp 1$，因此，作为与 $j^{\prime}$ 和 $j^{\prime \prime}$ 互补的定义，指标 $j^{\prime \prime \prime}$ 等于 $j^{\prime} \pm 1=j$，而作为与 $j$ 和 $j^{\prime \prime}$ 互补的定义，指标 $j^{\prime \prime \prime}$ 等于 $j^{\prime}$。结果，方程 $\left({ }^{* * * *}\right)$ 简化为

$$
\hat{A}_{j j^{\prime}}=-2 \hbar^{2} \varepsilon_{(j^{\prime} \mp 1)(j^{\prime} \pm 1) j^{\prime}} \varepsilon_{(j^{\prime} \mp 1)(j^{\prime} \pm 1) j^{\prime}} \hat{r}_{j} \hat{r}_{j^{\prime}}=-2 \hbar^{2} \hat{r}_{j} \hat{r}_{j^{\prime}}, \quad \text { for } j \neq j^{\prime}
$$

上述两个结果可以总结为

$$
\hat{A}_{j j^{\prime}}=2 \hbar^{2}\left(\hat{r}^{2} \delta_{j j^{\prime}}-\hat{r}_{j} \hat{r}_{j^{\prime}}\right)
$$

读者可能注意到了这个最终结果与刚体的惯性张量的一个微元 $d m$ 对其贡献的经典表达式之间的有趣类比 ${ }^{43}$：

$$
d I_{j j^{\prime}}=d m\left(r^{2} \delta_{j j^{\prime}}-r_{j} r_{j^{\prime}}\right)
$$

question: A time-independent force $\mathbf{F}=\mu\left(\mathbf{n}_{x} y+\mathbf{n}_{y} x\right)$, where $\mu$ is a small constant, is applied to a 3D harmonic oscillator of mass $m$ and frequency $\omega_{0}$. Calculate, in the first order of the perturbation theory, the effect of the force upon the ground state energy of the oscillator, and its lowest excited energy level. How small should the constant $\mu$ be for your results to be quantitatively correct?
solution:
Any potential force $\mathbf{F}=\mathbf{F}(\mathbf{r})$ may be described by an additional potential energy $U(\mathbf{r})$, such that $\mathbf{F}=-\nabla U$. In our particular case, independent integrations of the force $\mathbf{F}$ along each of three coordinates yield the results

$$
\begin{aligned}
& U=-\int F_{x} d x+f_{1}(y, z)=-\int \mu y d x+f_{1}(y, z)=-\mu x y+f_{1}(y, z) \\
& U=-\int F_{y} d y+f_{2}(x, z)=-\int \mu x d y+f_{2}(y, z)=-\mu x y+f_{2}(x, z) \\
& U=-\int F_{z} d z+f_{3}(x, y)=-\int 0 d z+f_{3}(x, y)=f_{3}(x, y)
\end{aligned}
$$

which are compatible only if $f_{3}(x, y)=-\mu x y+$ const, and $f_{1}(y, z)=f_{2}(x, z)=$ const. Dropping this inconsequential constant, we may use the resulting $U$ as the perturbation Hamiltonian:

$$
\hat{H}^{(1)}=-\mu x y
$$

As was discussed in the beginning of section 3.5 of the lecture notes, unperturbed eigenstates of the 3D oscillator may be described by the products of eigenfunctions of 1D similar harmonic oscillators:

$$
\psi_{k l m}^{(0)}(\mathbf{r})=\psi_{k}(x) \psi_{l}(y) \psi_{m}(z)
$$

with each of the indices $\{k, l, m\}$ taking independent integer values $0,1,2, \ldots$ The corresponding unperturbed energies are

$$
E_{k l m}^{(0)}=\hbar \omega_{0}\left(k+l+m+\frac{3}{2}\right)
$$

so that there is only one ground state with the wavefunction $\psi_{000}$ and energy $E_{0}=$ $(3 / 2) \hbar \omega_{0}$, and 3 lowest excited states with wavefunctions $\psi_{100}, \psi_{010}$, and $\psi_{001}$, all with the same energy $E_{1}=(5 / 2) \hbar \omega_{0}$.

According to Eq. (2.275), the non-degenerate ground state of the oscillator is described by an even function of all its arguments:

$$
\psi_{000}^{(0)}(\mathbf{r})=\psi_{0}(x) \psi_{0}(y) \psi_{0}(z) \propto \exp \left\{-\frac{x^{2}+y^{2}+z^{2}}{2 x_{0}^{2}}\right\}, \quad \text { with } x_{0} \equiv\left(\frac{\hbar}{m \omega_{0}}\right)^{1 / 2}
$$

so that the first-order shift (6.14) of its energy,
$$
E_{000}^{(1)}=\int_{-\infty}^{+\infty} d x \int_{-\infty}^{+\infty} d y \int_{-\infty}^{+\infty} d z \psi_{000}^{(0)^{*}}(\mathbf{r}) \hat{H}^{(1)} \psi_{000}^{(0)}(\mathbf{r})
$$

vanishes for the perturbation (*), which is an odd function of $x$ and $y$.
Similarly, all diagonal matrix elements (6.8) for the lowest excited states vanish as well, because $\psi_{100}, \psi_{010}$, and $\psi_{001}$ are odd functions of one coordinate, but even functions of the other two coordinates. For example, according to Eqs. (2.282) and (2.284),

$$
\psi_{100}(\mathbf{r})=\psi_{1}(x) \psi_{0}(y) \psi_{0}(z)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2} \pi^{3 / 4} x_{0}^{3 / 2}} \frac{2 x}{x_{0}} \exp \left\{-\frac{x^{2}+y^{2}+z^{2}}{2 x_{0}^{2}}\right\}
$$

so that

$$
E_{100}^{(1)}=\int_{-\infty}^{+\infty} d x \int_{-\infty}^{+\infty} d y \int_{-\infty}^{+\infty} d z \psi_{100}^{(0)^{*}}(\mathbf{r}) \hat{H}^{(1)} \psi_{100}^{(0)}(\mathbf{r}) \propto \int_{-\infty}^{+\infty} y \exp \left\{-\frac{y^{2}}{x_{0}^{2}}\right\} d y=0
$$

and similarly for two other eigenstates.
However, since the excited eigenstates are degenerate, their mixed matrix elements are also important, and one pair of these elements (not involving the eigenfunction $\psi_{001}$ ) is different from zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}
H_{100,010}^{(1)} & =\int_{-\infty}^{+\infty} d x \int_{-\infty}^{+\infty} d y \int_{-\infty}^{+\infty} d z \psi_{100}^{(0)^{*}}(\mathbf{r}) \hat{H}^{(1)} \psi_{010}^{(0)}(\mathbf{r}) \\
& =-\mu \int_{-\infty}^{+\infty} d x \int_{-\infty}^{+\infty} d y \int_{-\infty}^{+\infty} d z \quad \psi_{1}^{*}(x) \psi_{0}^{*}(y) \psi_{1}^{*}(z) x y \psi_{0}(x) \psi_{1}(y) \psi_{0}(z) \\
& =-\mu \frac{1}{2 \pi^{3 / 2} x_{0}^{3}} \int_{-\infty}^{+\infty} d x \int_{-\infty}^{+\infty} d y \int_{-\infty}^{+\infty} d z \quad x y \frac{2 x}{x_{0}} \frac{2 y}{x_{0}} \exp \left\{-\frac{x^{2}+y^{2}+z^{2}}{x_{0}^{2}}\right\} \\
& =-\mu \frac{2 x_{0}^{2}}{\pi^{3 / 2}}\left(\int_{-\infty}^{+\infty} \xi^{2} \exp \left\{-\xi^{2}\right\} d \xi\right)^{2}\left(\int_{-\infty}^{+\infty} \exp \left\{-\xi^{2}\right\} d \xi\right)
\end{aligned}
$$

These are two standard Gaussian integrals equal, respectively, to $\pi^{1 / 2} / 2$ and $\pi^{1 / 2}$, so that

$$
H_{100,010}^{(1)}=-\frac{\mu x_{0}^{2}}{2} \equiv-\frac{\mu \hbar}{2 m \omega_{0}}
$$

and absolutely similarly for $H^{(1)}_{010,100}$.
Hence the characteristic equation (6.26) for the states $\{100\}$ and $\{010\}$ has the form

$$
\left|\begin{array}{cc}
H_{100,100}^{(1)}-E^{(1)} & H_{010,100}^{(1)} \\
H_{100,010}^{(1)} & H_{010,010}^{(1)}-E^{(1)}
\end{array}\right| \equiv\left|\begin{array}{cc}
-E^{(1)} & -\mu \hbar / 2 m \omega_{0} \\
-\mu \hbar / 2 m \omega_{0} & -E^{(1)}
\end{array}\right|=0
$$
and has two roots

$$
E_{ \pm}^{(1)}= \pm \frac{\mu \hbar}{2 m \omega_{0}}
$$

Their difference describes lifting the degeneracy of these two states, while the state $\{001\}$ is not involved in the interaction, and its energy is not changed.

The above calculation is asymptotically exact if the energy correction is much smaller than the basic level spacing $\hbar \omega_{0}$:

$$
\left|\frac{\mu \hbar}{2 m \omega_{0}}\right| \ll \hbar \omega_{0}, \quad \text { i.e. if }|\mu| \ll 2 m \omega_{0}^{2}
$$

Note the Planck constant has dropped from this condition, so it has a classical character. This happens because the perturbation is a quadratic form of the coordinates, just as the unperturbed potential energy of the oscillator,

$$
U^{(0)}=\frac{m \omega_{0}^{2}}{2}\left(x^{2}+y^{2}+z^{2}\right)
$$

so that the relation of their magnitudes does not depend on the oscillator's quantum length scale $x_{0}$. This fact also allows an exact solution of this problem, similar to that of problem 3.16. The reader is challenged to carry out such solution, and compare the result with the above equation.

question: 一个时间不变的力$\mathbf{F}=\mu\left(\mathbf{n}_{x} y+\mathbf{n}_{y} x\right)$，其中$\mu$是一个小常数，施加在质量为$m$且频率为$\omega_{0}$的三维谐振子上。计算在微扰理论的一阶近似中，该力对振子的基态能量及其最低激发能级的影响。为了使你的结果在量值上正确，常数$\mu$应当有多小？
solution:
任何势力 $\mathbf{F}=\mathbf{F}(\mathbf{r})$ 都可以通过一个附加的势能 $U(\mathbf{r})$ 来描述，使得 $\mathbf{F}=-\nabla U$。在我们的特定情况下，沿着三个坐标分别对力 $\mathbf{F}$ 进行独立积分得到以下结果

$$
\begin{aligned}
& U=-\int F_{x} d x+f_{1}(y, z)=-\int \mu y d x+f_{1}(y, z)=-\mu x y+f_{1}(y, z) \\
& U=-\int F_{y} d y+f_{2}(x, z)=-\int \mu x d y+f_{2}(y, z)=-\mu x y+f_{2}(x, z) \\
& U=-\int F_{z} d z+f_{3}(x, y)=-\int 0 d z+f_{3}(x, y)=f_{3}(x, y)
\end{aligned}
$$

这些结果只有在 $f_{3}(x, y)=-\mu x y+$ 常数，并且 $f_{1}(y, z)=f_{2}(x, z)=$ 常数时才兼容。去掉这个无关紧要的常数，我们可以将得到的 $U$ 用作微扰哈密顿量：

$$
\hat{H}^{(1)}=-\mu x y
$$

如在讲义第3.5节开头所讨论的，未受扰动的三维振子的本征态可以通过一维相似简谐振子的本征函数的乘积来描述：

$$
\psi_{k l m}^{(0)}(\mathbf{r})=\psi_{k}(x) \psi_{l}(y) \psi_{m}(z)
$$

其中每个指标 $\{k, l, m\}$ 取独立的整数值 $0,1,2, \ldots$。相应的未受扰动的能量为

$$
E_{k l m}^{(0)}=\hbar \omega_{0}\left(k+l+m+\frac{3}{2}\right)
$$

因此，只有一个基态，其波函数为 $\psi_{000}$，能量为 $E_{0}=$ $(3 / 2) \hbar \omega_{0}$，并且有三个最低激发态，其波函数为 $\psi_{100}, \psi_{010}$ 和 $\psi_{001}$，它们的能量相同，均为 $E_{1}=(5 / 2) \hbar \omega_{0}$。

根据方程 (2.275)，振子的非简并基态由其所有参数的偶函数描述：

$$
\psi_{000}^{(0)}(\mathbf{r})=\psi_{0}(x) \psi_{0}(y) \psi_{0}(z) \propto \exp \left\{-\frac{x^{2}+y^{2}+z^{2}}{2 x_{0}^{2}}\right\}, \quad \text { with } x_{0} \equiv\left(\frac{\hbar}{m \omega_{0}}\right)^{1 / 2}
$$

因此，其能量的一阶修正 (6.14)，

$$
E_{000}^{(1)}=\int_{-\infty}^{+\infty} d x \int_{-\infty}^{+\infty} d y \int_{-\infty}^{+\infty} d z \psi_{000}^{(0)^{*}}(\mathbf{r}) \hat{H}^{(1)} \psi_{000}^{(0)}(\mathbf{r})
$$

对于微扰 (*) 为零，因为它是 $x$ 和 $y$ 的奇函数。同样，所有最低激发态的对角矩阵元 (6.8) 也为零，因为 $\psi_{100}, \psi_{010}$ 和 $\psi_{001}$ 是一个坐标的奇函数，而是另两个坐标的偶函数。例如，根据方程 (2.282) 和 (2.284)，

$$
\psi_{100}(\mathbf{r})=\psi_{1}(x) \psi_{0}(y) \psi_{0}(z)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2} \pi^{3 / 4} x_{0}^{3 / 2}} \frac{2 x}{x_{0}} \exp \left\{-\frac{x^{2}+y^{2}+z^{2}}{2 x_{0}^{2}}\right\}
$$

因此

$$
E_{100}^{(1)}=\int_{-\infty}^{+\infty} d x \int_{-\infty}^{+\infty} d y \int_{-\infty}^{+\infty} d z \psi_{100}^{(0)^{*}}(\mathbf{r}) \hat{H}^{(1)} \psi_{100}^{(0)}(\mathbf{r}) \propto \int_{-\infty}^{+\infty} y \exp \left\{-\frac{y^{2}}{x_{0}^{2}}\right\} d y=0
$$

对于另外两个本征态也是如此。
然而，由于激发本征态是简并的，它们的混合矩阵元也很重要，其中有一对矩阵元（不涉及本征函数 $\psi_{001}$）不为零：

$$
\begin{aligned}
H_{100,010}^{(1)} & =\int_{-\infty}^{+\infty} d x \int_{-\infty}^{+\infty} d y \int_{-\infty}^{+\infty} d z \psi_{100}^{(0)^{*}}(\mathbf{r}) \hat{H}^{(1)} \psi_{010}^{(0)}(\mathbf{r}) \\
& =-\mu \int_{-\infty}^{+\infty} d x \int_{-\infty}^{+\infty} d y \int_{-\infty}^{+\infty} d z \quad \psi_{1}^{*}(x) \psi_{0}^{*}(y) \psi_{1}^{*}(z) x y \psi_{0}(x) \psi_{1}(y) \psi_{0}(z) \\
& =-\mu \frac{1}{2 \pi^{3 / 2} x_{0}^{3}} \int_{-\infty}^{+\infty} d x \int_{-\infty}^{+\infty} d y \int_{-\infty}^{+\infty} d z \quad x y \frac{2 x}{x_{0}} \frac{2 y}{x_{0}} \exp \left\{-\frac{x^{2}+y^{2}+z^{2}}{x_{0}^{2}}\right\} \\
& =-\mu \frac{2 x_{0}^{2}}{\pi^{3 / 2}}\left(\int_{-\infty}^{+\infty} \xi^{2} \exp \left\{-\xi^{2}\right\} d \xi\right)^{2}\left(\int_{-\infty}^{+\infty} \exp \left\{-\xi^{2}\right\} d \xi\right)
\end{aligned}
$$

这些是两个标准的高斯积分，分别等于 $\pi^{1 / 2} / 2$ 和 $\pi^{1 / 2}$，所以

$$
H_{100,010}^{(1)}=-\frac{\mu x_{0}^{2}}{2} \equiv-\frac{\mu \hbar}{2 m \omega_{0}}
$$

对于 $H^{(1)}_{010,100}$ 也是完全相同的。
因此，对于态 $\{100\}$ 和 $\{010\}$ 的特征方程 (6.26) 具有形式

$$
\left|\begin{array}{cc}
H_{100,100}^{(1)}-E^{(1)} & H_{010,100}^{(1)} \\
H_{100,010}^{(1)} & H_{010,010}^{(1)}-E^{(1)}
\end{array}\right| \equiv\left|\begin{array}{cc}
-E^{(1)} & -\mu \hbar / 2 m \omega_{0} \\
-\mu \hbar / 2 m \omega_{0} & -E^{(1)}
\end{array}\right|=0
$$
并有两个根

$$
E_{ \pm}^{(1)}= \pm \frac{\mu \hbar}{2 m \omega_{0}}
$$

它们的差异描述了这两个态的简并解除，而态 $\{001\}$ 未参与相互作用，其能量未改变。

如果能量修正远小于基本能级间隔 $\hbar \omega_{0}$，则上述计算是渐进精确的：

$$
\left|\frac{\mu \hbar}{2 m \omega_{0}}\right| \ll \hbar \omega_{0}, \quad \text { i.e. if }|\mu| \ll 2 m \omega_{0}^{2}
$$

请注意，普朗克常数从这个条件中消失了，因此它具有经典特性。这是因为微扰是坐标的二次型，正如振子的未受扰动的势能，

$$
U^{(0)}=\frac{m \omega_{0}^{2}}{2}\left(x^{2}+y^{2}+z^{2}\right)
$$

因此，它们的大小关系不依赖于振子的量子长度尺度 $x_{0}$。这一事实也允许对这个问题进行精确解答，类似于问题3.16。读者被挑战去完成这样的解答，并将结果与上述方程进行比较。

question:
(i) Calculate, in the lowest nonvanishing order of the perturbation theory, the probability that the pulse drives the oscillator into its lowest excited state.
(ii) Compare the result with the exact solution of the problem.
(iii) Spell out the perturbative result for a Gaussian-shaped waveform,

$$
F(t)=F_{0} \exp \left\{-t^{2} / \tau^{2}\right\}
$$

and analyze its dependence on the time scale $\tau$ of the pulse.
solution:
(i) The general approach to such problems is given by the set of (exact!) Eqs. (6.84) of the lecture notes. As was argued at the derivation of Eq. (6.90) (for a specific time dependence of the perturbation), in the lowest order of the perturbation theory we may leave, on the right-hand sides of these equations, only the terms whose probability amplitudes $a_{n^{\prime}}$ are initially different from zero. In our current problem this is only the ground-state amplitude, $a_{0}=1$, so that the right-hand side of each Eq. (6.84), with $n^{\prime}=0$, is reduced to just one term:

$$
i \hbar \dot{a}_{n}=H_{n 0}^{(1)}(t) e^{i \omega_{n 0} t}$$

Just as was repeatedly discussed in this course, a weak, coordinate-independent force $F(t)$ may be described by the following Hamiltonian's perturbation,

$$
\hat{H}^{(1)}(t)=-F(t) \hat{x}
$$

so that Eq. $\left({ }^{*}\right)$ takes the form

$$
i \hbar \dot{a}_{n}=-F(t) x_{n 0} e^{i \omega_{n 0} t}$$

where $x_{n 0}$ are the matrix elements of the coordinate operator in the unperturbed brackets-see Eq. (6.8). As Eq. (5.92) of the lecture notes shows, for a harmonic oscillator all such matrix elements equal zero, with just one exception:

$$
x_{n 0}=\left(\frac{\hbar}{2 m \omega_{0}}\right)^{1 / 2} \times \begin{cases}1, & \text { for } n=1 \\ 0, & \text { otherwise }\end{cases}
$$

so that only one of all Eqs. $\left({ }^{*}\right)$, with $n=1$, has a nonvanishing right-hand side:

$$
i \hbar \dot{a}_{1}=-\left(\frac{\hbar}{2 m \omega_{0}}\right)^{1 / 2} F(t) e^{i \omega_{0} t}$$

where Eq. (5.75) has been used to spell out the quantum transition frequency: $\omega_{10} \equiv \left(E_{1}-E_{0}\right) / \hbar=\omega_{0}$.

This differential equation for amplitude $a_{1}(t)$, with the initial condition $a_{1}(-\infty)=0$, may be readily integrated to find its final value:

$$
a_{1}(+\infty)=i\left(\frac{1}{2 m \hbar \omega_{0}}\right)^{1 / 2} \int_{-\infty}^{+\infty} F(t) e^{i \omega_{0} t} d t
$$

From here, the probability of the oscillator's excitation by the pulse is

$$
W_{1}(+\infty) \equiv\left|a_{1}(+\infty)\right|^{2}=\frac{|I|^{2}}{2 m \hbar \omega_{0}}, \quad \text { where } I \equiv \int_{-\infty}^{+\infty} F(t) e^{i \omega_{0} t} d t
$$

This integral converges for any pulse of a finite duration, i.e. if $F(t) \rightarrow 0$ at $t \rightarrow \pm \infty$.

(ii) Due to our initial assumptions, the above formulas are only valid if $\left|a_{1}(t)\right|^{2} \ll 1$ for all $t$, in particular, if $W_{1}(+\infty) \ll 1$, i.e. if

$$
|I|^{2} \ll 2 m \hbar \omega_{0}
$$

As was discussed in the model solution of problem 6.16, for this particular system (the harmonic oscillator, initially in the ground state), the exact solution, valid for any $W_{1}$, is also possible:

$$
W_{1}=\langle n\rangle e^{-\langle n\rangle} \equiv \frac{|I|^{2}}{2 m \hbar \omega_{0}} \exp \left\{-\frac{|I|^{2}}{2 m \hbar \omega_{0}}\right\}
$$

If the condition $\left({ }^{* * * *}\right)$ is satisfied, this formula duly reduces to the perturbative result $\left({ }^{* * *}\right)$.

(iii) For the particular pulse shape given in the assignment, $I$ is a standard Gaussian integral, which may be readily worked out as was discussed in section 2.2 of the lecture notes - see Eqs. (2.21)-(2.23):

$$
\begin{aligned}
I= & F_{0} \int_{-\infty}^{+\infty} \exp \left\{-\frac{t^{2}}{\tau^{2}}+i \omega_{0} t\right\} d t=F_{0} \exp \left\{\left(\frac{-i \omega_{0} \tau}{2}\right)^{2}\right\} \\
& \times \int_{-\infty}^{+\infty} \exp \left\{-\left[\left(\frac{t}{\tau}\right)^{2}+2\left(\frac{t}{\tau}\right)\left(\frac{-i \omega_{0} \tau}{2}\right)+\left(\frac{-i \omega_{0} \tau}{2}\right)^{2}\right]\right\} d t \\
= & F_{0} \exp \left\{-\frac{\omega_{0}^{2} \tau^{2}}{4}\right\} \int_{-\infty}^{+\infty} \exp \left\{-\left[\frac{t}{\tau}+\frac{-i \omega_{0} \tau}{2}\right]^{2}\right\} d t \\
= & \pi^{1 / 2} F_{0} \tau \exp \left\{-\frac{\omega_{0}^{2} \tau^{2}}{4}\right\}
\end{aligned}
$$

so that, finally, the probability of the oscillator's excitation is

$$
W_{1}(+\infty)=\frac{|I|^{2}}{2 m \hbar \omega_{0}}=\frac{\pi F_{0}^{2} \tau^{2}}{2 m \hbar \omega_{0}} \exp \left\{-\frac{\omega_{0}^{2} \tau^{2}}{2}\right\}
$$

According to this formula, at fixed other parameters, the excitation is most effective if the pulse's duration is of the order of oscillator's period: $\tau_{\text {opt }}=\sqrt{ } 2 / \omega_{0}$. This is natural, because a much shorter pulse does not give the system enough time to accomplish the interlevel quantum transition, while a very long pulse is just an adiabatic change of an oscillator's parameter (namely, of its equilibrium position $X_{0}(t)=F(t) / m \omega_{0}{ }^{2}$ ) and, according to the discussion in the beginning of section 6.5 of the lecture notes (and in the solution of problem 6.16), leaves the system in the initial quantum state.

question:
(i) 计算在微扰理论的最低非消失阶中，脉冲将振荡器驱动到其最低激发态的概率。

(ii) 将结果与问题的精确解进行比较。

(iii) 写出高斯形波形的微扰结果，

$$
F(t)=F_{0} \exp \left\{-t^{2} / \tau^{2}\right\}
$$

并分析其对脉冲时间尺度 $\tau$ 的依赖性。
solution:
(i) 解决这类问题的一般方法由讲义中的（精确的！）方程(6.84)给出。正如在推导方程(6.90)时所论述的（针对扰动的特定时间依赖性），在最低阶的微扰理论中，我们可以在这些方程的右侧仅保留那些概率振幅$a_{n^{\prime}}$初始时不为零的项。在我们当前的问题中，这仅是基态振幅$a_{0}=1$，因此每个方程(6.84)的右侧，在$n^{\prime}=0$时，仅简化为一项：

$$
i \hbar \dot{a}_{n}=H_{n 0}^{(1)}(t) e^{i \omega_{n 0} t}$$

正如在本课程中反复讨论的，一个弱的、坐标无关的力$F(t)$可以通过以下哈密顿量的扰动来描述，

$$
\hat{H}^{(1)}(t)=-F(t) \hat{x}
$$

因此方程$\left({ }^{*}\right)$变为

$$
i \hbar \dot{a}_{n}=-F(t) x_{n 0} e^{i \omega_{n 0} t}$$

其中$x_{n 0}$是无扰动括号中的坐标算符的矩阵元素——参见方程(6.8)。正如讲义中的方程(5.92)所示，对于谐振子，所有这样的矩阵元素都等于零，只有一个例外：

$$
x_{n 0}=\left(\frac{\hbar}{2 m \omega_{0}}\right)^{1 / 2} \times \begin{cases}1, & \text { for } n=1 \\ 0, & \text { otherwise }\end{cases}
$$

因此，所有方程$\left({ }^{*}\right)$中，只有$n=1$的方程右侧不为零：

$$
i \hbar \dot{a}_{1}=-\left(\frac{\hbar}{2 m \omega_{0}}\right)^{1 / 2} F(t) e^{i \omega_{0} t}$$

其中使用了方程(5.75)来明确量子跃迁频率：$\omega_{10} \equiv \left(E_{1}-E_{0}\right) / \hbar=\omega_{0}$。

这个关于振幅$a_{1}(t)$的微分方程，初始条件为$a_{1}(-\infty)=0$，可以很容易地积分以找到其最终值：

$$
a_{1}(+\infty)=i\left(\frac{1}{2 m \hbar \omega_{0}}\right)^{1 / 2} \int_{-\infty}^{+\infty} F(t) e^{i \omega_{0} t} d t
$$

从这里，振子被脉冲激发的概率为

$$
W_{1}(+\infty) \equiv\left|a_{1}(+\infty)\right|^{2}=\frac{|I|^{2}}{2 m \hbar \omega_{0}}, \quad \text { where } I \equiv \int_{-\infty}^{+\infty} F(t) e^{i \omega_{0} t} d t
$$

对于任何有限持续时间的脉冲，这个积分是收敛的，即如果$F(t) \rightarrow 0$在$t \rightarrow \pm \infty$时。

(ii) 由于我们的初始假设，上述公式仅在$\left|a_{1}(t)\right|^{2} \ll 1$对于所有$t$时有效，特别是如果$W_{1}(+\infty) \ll 1$，即如果

$$
|I|^{2} \ll 2 m \hbar \omega_{0}
$$

正如在问题6.16的模型解中讨论的，对于这个特定系统（最初在基态的谐振子），也可以得到适用于任何$W_{1}$的精确解：

$$
W_{1}=\langle n\rangle e^{-\langle n\rangle} \equiv \frac{|I|^{2}}{2 m \hbar \omega_{0}} \exp \left\{-\frac{|I|^{2}}{2 m \hbar \omega_{0}}\right\}
$$

如果条件$\left({ }^{* * * *}\right)$满足，这个公式就会简化为微扰结果$\left({ }^{* * *}\right)$。

(iii) 对于作业中给出的特定脉冲形状，$I$是一个标准的高斯积分，可以按照讲义第2.2节中讨论的方法进行计算——参见方程(2.21)-(2.23)：

$$
\begin{aligned}
I= & F_{0} \int_{-\infty}^{+\infty} \exp \left\{-\frac{t^{2}}{\tau^{2}}+i \omega_{0} t\right\} d t=F_{0} \exp \left\{\left(\frac{-i \omega_{0} \tau}{2}\right)^{2}\right\} \\
& \times \int_{-\infty}^{+\infty} \exp \left\{-\left[\left(\frac{t}{\tau}\right)^{2}+2\left(\frac{t}{\tau}\right)\left(\frac{-i \omega_{0} \tau}{2}\right)+\left(\frac{-i \omega_{0} \tau}{2}\right)^{2}\right]\right\} d t \\
= & F_{0} \exp \left\{-\frac{\omega_{0}^{2} \tau^{2}}{4}\right\} \int_{-\infty}^{+\infty} \exp \left\{-\left[\frac{t}{\tau}+\frac{-i \omega_{0} \tau}{2}\right]^{2}\right\} d t \\
= & \pi^{1 / 2} F_{0} \tau \exp \left\{-\frac{\omega_{0}^{2} \tau^{2}}{4}\right\}
\end{aligned}
$$

因此，最终，振子激发的概率为

$$
W_{1}(+\infty)=\frac{|I|^{2}}{2 m \hbar \omega_{0}}=\frac{\pi F_{0}^{2} \tau^{2}}{2 m \hbar \omega_{0}} \exp \left\{-\frac{\omega_{0}^{2} \tau^{2}}{2}\right\}
$$

根据这个公式，在固定其他参数的情况下，激发最有效的是当脉冲的持续时间与振子的周期相当时：$\tau_{\text {opt }}=\sqrt{ } 2 / \omega_{0}$。这很自然，因为一个更短的脉冲没有给系统足够的时间来完成能级间的量子跃迁，而一个非常长的脉冲只是振子参数（即其平衡位置$X_{0}(t)=F(t) / m \omega_{0}{ }^{2}$）的绝热变化，并且根据讲义第6.5节开头的讨论（以及问题6.16的解），会使系统保持在初始量子态。

question: A small body is dropped down to the surface of Earth from height $h \ll R_{\mathrm{E}}$, without initial velocity. Calculate the magnitude and direction of its deviation from the vertical line, due to the Earth's rotation. Estimate the effect's magnitude for a body dropped from the top floor of the Empire State Building.
solution:
The Earth's rotational effects are relatively weak, $R_{\mathrm{E}} \omega_{\mathrm{E}}^{2} \ll g$, so that we can analyze them as small perturbations of a purely vertical fall, with the velocity changing as $v_{z}(t)=-g t$, and the drop time $\Delta t=(2 h / g)^{1 / 2}$. With the $v_{z}$-component dominating the body's velocity $\mathbf{v}$, the Coriolis force $\mathbf{F}_{\mathrm{C}}=-2 m\left(\omega_{\mathrm{E}} \times \mathbf{v}\right)$ is directed horizontally (in the Northern hemisphere, eastward), so that the deviation $x$ in that direction obeys equation

$$
m \ddot{x}=-2 m \omega_{\mathrm{E}} v_{z}(t) \sin \theta=2 m \omega_{\mathrm{E}} g t \sin \theta
$$

where $\theta$ is the polar angle (complementary to the geographic latitude) of the experiment's location. Integrating the equation over time twice, with zero initial conditions for both $x$ and $v_{x}$, we obtain

$$
v_{x}(t)=\omega_{\mathrm{E}} g t^{2} \sin \theta, \quad x(t)=\omega_{\mathrm{E}} g \frac{t^{3}}{3} \sin \theta
$$

so that the final eastward deviation is

$$
d_{\mathrm{E}} \equiv x(\Delta t)=\frac{1}{3} \omega_{\mathrm{E}} g\left(\frac{2 h}{g}\right)^{3 / 2} \sin \theta
$$

The centrifugal force $\mathbf{F}_{\mathrm{c}}=-m \omega_{\mathrm{E}} \times\left(\omega_{\mathrm{E}} \times \mathbf{r}\right)$, is perpendicular to the polar axis, i.e., has both horizontal and vertical components, but the latter gives just a small correction to the flight time. The horizontal (meridional) component $\left(\mathbf{F}_{\mathrm{c}}\right)_{y}=-F_{\mathrm{c}} \cos \theta=-\left(m \omega_{\mathrm{E}}^{2} R_{\mathrm{E}} \sin \theta\right) \cos \theta$, is virtually constant in time, so that the corresponding equation of motion in the meridional direction,

$$
m \ddot{y}=-m \omega_{\mathrm{E}}^{2} R_{\mathrm{E}} \sin \theta \cos \theta=\text { const }
$$

has a well-known solution

$$
y(t)=-\omega_{\mathrm{E}}^{2} R_{\mathrm{E}} \sin \theta \cos \theta \frac{t^{2}}{2}
$$

and the final southward deviation is

$$
d_{\mathrm{S}} \equiv-y(\Delta t)=\omega_{\mathrm{E}}^{2} R_{\mathrm{E}} \sin \theta \cos \theta \frac{h}{g}
$$

For our parameters, $\omega_{\mathrm{E}} \approx 0.73 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{~s}^{-1}, R_{\mathrm{E}} \approx 6.4 \times 10^{6} \mathrm{~m}, g \approx 9.8 \mathrm{~m} \mathrm{~s}^{-2}, \theta \approx 49.5^{\circ}$, and $h=373 \mathrm{~m}$ (the top floor of the Empire State Building), the southward deviation is very substantial, $d_{\mathrm{S}} \approx 63 \mathrm{~cm}$. However, it has to be measured from the direction toward the center of the sphere that the Earth would be without its rotation, rather than from the static position of a vertically hanging pendulum. (The latter aligns itself with the 'net force' $\mathbf{F}=\mathbf{m g}-m \omega_{\mathrm{E}} \times\left(\omega_{\mathrm{E}} \times \mathbf{r}\right)$, so that from this direction, the falling body does not deviate to either North or South.) This is why the velocity-dependent eastward deviation $d_{\mathrm{E}}$, due to the Coriolis force, is easier to measure, although it is smaller, for our parameters $d_{\mathrm{E}} \approx 12 \mathrm{~cm}$.

question: 一个小物体从高度$h \ll R_{\mathrm{E}}$处无初速度下落到地球表面。计算由于地球自转导致的物体偏离垂直线的大小和方向。估算从帝国大厦顶层下落的物体的偏移量。
solution:
地球的自转效应相对较弱，$R_{\mathrm{E}} \omega_{\mathrm{E}}^{2} \ll g$，因此我们可以将其视为纯粹垂直下落的小扰动来分析，其中速度随时间变化为$v_{z}(t)=-g t$，下落时间$\Delta t=(2 h / g)^{1 / 2}$。由于$v_{z}$分量在物体速度$\mathbf{v}$中占主导地位，科里奥利力$\mathbf{F}_{\mathrm{C}}=-2 m\left(\omega_{\mathrm{E}} \times \mathbf{v}\right)$指向水平方向（在北半球向东），因此该方向上的偏差$x$满足方程

$$
m \ddot{x}=-2 m \omega_{\mathrm{E}} v_{z}(t) \sin \theta=2 m \omega_{\mathrm{E}} g t \sin \theta
$$

其中$\theta$是实验地点的极角（地理纬度的余角）。将方程在时间上积分两次，且初始条件为$x$和$v_{x}$均为零，我们得到

$$
v_{x}(t)=\omega_{\mathrm{E}} g t^{2} \sin \theta, \quad x(t)=\omega_{\mathrm{E}} g \frac{t^{3}}{3} \sin \theta
$$

因此最终的向东偏差为

$$
d_{\mathrm{E}} \equiv x(\Delta t)=\frac{1}{3} \omega_{\mathrm{E}} g\left(\frac{2 h}{g}\right)^{3 / 2} \sin \theta
$$

离心力$\mathbf{F}_{\mathrm{c}}=-m \omega_{\mathrm{E}} \times\left(\omega_{\mathrm{E}} \times \mathbf{r}\right)$垂直于极轴，即具有水平和垂直分量，但后者对飞行时间仅有微小修正。水平（子午）分量$\left(\mathbf{F}_{\mathrm{c}}\right)_{y}=-F_{\mathrm{c}} \cos \theta=-\left(m \omega_{\mathrm{E}}^{2} R_{\mathrm{E}} \sin \theta\right) \cos \theta$在时间上几乎是恒定的，因此在子午方向上的运动方程为

$$
m \ddot{y}=-m \omega_{\mathrm{E}}^{2} R_{\mathrm{E}} \sin \theta \cos \theta=\text { const }
$$

具有众所周知的解

$$
y(t)=-\omega_{\mathrm{E}}^{2} R_{\mathrm{E}} \sin \theta \cos \theta \frac{t^{2}}{2}
$$

最终的向南偏差为

$$
d_{\mathrm{S}} \equiv-y(\Delta t)=\omega_{\mathrm{E}}^{2} R_{\mathrm{E}} \sin \theta \cos \theta \frac{h}{g}
$$

对于我们的参数，$\omega_{\mathrm{E}} \approx 0.73 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{~s}^{-1}, R_{\mathrm{E}} \approx 6.4 \times 10^{6} \mathrm{~m}, g \approx 9.8 \mathrm{~m} \mathrm{~s}^{-2}, \theta \approx 49.5^{\circ}$，和$h=373 \mathrm{~m}$（帝国大厦的顶层），向南的偏差是非常显著的，$d_{\mathrm{S}} \approx 63 \mathrm{~cm}$。然而，它必须从地球不自转时将成为的球体中心方向进行测量，而不是从静止悬挂的垂线的位置测量。（后者使其自身与“净力”$\mathbf{F}=\mathbf{m g}-m \omega_{\mathrm{E}} \times\left(\omega_{\mathrm{E}} \times \mathbf{r}\right)$对齐，因此从这个方向看，坠落的物体不会偏向北或南。）这就是为什么由于科里奥利力导致的速度相关的向东偏差$d_{\mathrm{E}}$更容易测量，尽管它较小，对于我们的参数$d_{\mathrm{E}} \approx 12 \mathrm{~cm}$。

question:
Derive a 2D differential equation describing the propagation of relatively long $(\lambda \gg h)$ waves on the surface of a broad, plane layer of thickness $h$, of an ideal, incompressible fluid, and use it to calculate the longest standing wave modes and frequencies in a layer covering a spherical planet of radius $R \gg h$.

Hint: The last task requires some familiarity with the basic properties of spherical harmonics ${ }^{16}$.
solution:
Solution: First let us consider a plane layer. Then, generalizing the approach discussed in section 8.4 of the lecture notes, and in the model solution of problem 8.9 , we may look for a solution of the Euler equation (8.26) in the form

[^0]
[^0]:    ${ }^{15}$ See, e.g. Eq. (A.24) with $d f / d  
 $$
F_{\omega}(\theta, \varphi+2 \pi)=F_{\omega}(\theta, \varphi)
$$

where $\theta$ and $\varphi$ are the usual spherical coordinates (with $0 \leqslant \theta \leqslant \pi$ ). In these coordinates, Eq. $\left({ }^{* * *}\right)$ takes the form ${ }^{18}$

$$
\frac{1}{R^{2}}\left[\frac{1}{\sin \theta} \frac{\partial}{\partial \theta}\left(\sin \theta \frac{\partial}{\partial \theta}\right)+\frac{1}{\sin ^{2} \theta} \frac{\partial^{2}}{\partial \varphi^{2}}\right] F_{\omega}+k^{2} F_{\omega}=0
$$

The eigenfunctions of this equation, with the periodicity $\left({ }^{* * * *}\right)$, are either the so-called spherical harmonics $Y_{l}^{m}(\theta, \varphi)$, or their real linear combinations $Y_{l m}(\theta, \varphi)$, with integer numbers $l$ and $m$ (restricted by relations $l \geqslant 0$, and $-l \leqslant m \leqslant+l$ ); ${ }^{19}$ the corresponding eigenvalues of $k^{2}$ are

$$
k_{l}^{2}=\frac{l(l+1)}{R^{2}}, \quad \text { so that } \omega_{l}=v k_{l}=\frac{v}{R}[l(l+1)]^{1 / 2}
$$

(As this formula shows, the eigenvalues are independent on $m$, i.e. are ( $2 l+1$ )degenerate.)

However, not all these modes of this spectrum may be implemented for the surface waves, because the fluid's incompressibility (i.e. the fluid volume conservation) imposes the following additional restriction on the surface displacement $\left(q_{y}\right)_{\omega} \propto \operatorname{Re}\left[F_{\omega}\right]$ :

$$
\oint_{4 \pi}\left(q_{y}\right)_{\omega} d \Omega \equiv \int_{0}^{\pi} \sin \theta d \theta \int_{0}^{2 \pi} d \varphi\left(q_{y}\right)_{\omega}=0
$$

This requirement bans the lowest mode with $l=m=0$ (with $Y_{0}^{0}(\theta, \varphi)=Y_{00}(\theta, \varphi)=$ const), which would correspond to a uniform swelling of the fluid layer and have the frequency $\omega_{0}=0$; all other modes satisfy this requirement. Hence the lowestfrequency standing waves are the three modes with $l=1$, and $m=-1,0$, and +1 , which may be selected, for example, in the form

$$
Y_{10}=a \cos \theta, \quad Y_{1(+1)}=a \sin \theta \cos \varphi, \quad Y_{1(-1)}=a \sin \theta \sin \varphi
$$

(Since these standing waves differ only by their spatial orientation ${ }^{20}$, and have the same frequency $\omega_{1}=\sqrt{2} v / R$, any of their linear combinations also describes a possible standing wave.) Note that a 'plane' wave (with not only $k=$ const, but also $\mathbf{k}=$ const), with the corresponding value of the wave number, $k_{1}=\sqrt{2} / R$, would have wavelength $\lambda_{1}=2 \pi / k_{1}=\sqrt{2} \pi R \approx 4.44 R$-rather than $2 \pi R$ as one could naively conjecture ignoring sphere's curvature.

If this simple model is applied to the Earth's oceans, taking $R=R_{\mathrm{E}} \approx 6.37 \times 10^{6} \mathrm{~m}$, $g \approx 9.8 \mathrm{~m} \mathrm{~s}^{-2}$, and $h$ equal to oceans' average depth of $3.7 \times 10^{3} \mathrm{~m}$ (thus completely ignoring the scattering effects of the land masses), it gives $v \approx 190 \mathrm{~m} \mathrm{~s}^{-1}$ and $\omega_{1} \approx 4.2 \times 10^{-5} \mathrm{~s}^{-1}$, corresponding to the time period $\mathscr{T}_{1} \equiv 2 \pi / \omega_{1} \approx 1.5 \times 10^{5} \mathrm{~s} \approx$ 41 h . Note, however, that the calculation of the wave's attenuation due to the water's

    ${ }^{19}$ See, e.g. Part QM section 3.6. In particular, the explicit expressions for the harmonics with the lowest $l$, and hence the lowest $k$, are listed in Part QM Eqs. (3.174)-(3.176).
    ${ }^{20}$ See, e.g. the second row in Part QM figure 3.20.

Problem 8.12. Calculate the velocity distribution and the dispersion relation of the waves propagating along the horizontal interface of two thick layers of ideal, incompressible, non-mixing fluids of different densities.

Solution: Since the equation describing the fluid dynamics inside each fluid (located, say, below and above the horizontal plane $y=0$ ), the wave structure is the same as on the surface of a single fluid (see section 8.4 of the lecture notes, in particular figure 8.7 and Eq. (8.42)) with the amplitude decaying into each fluid:

$$
\phi_{\mathrm{e}}=\operatorname{Re}\left[\Phi_{\mathrm{e}} e^{i(k z-\omega t) \tau k y}\right]
$$

where the upper sign refers to the top fluid (located at $y>0$ ), and the lower sign to the bottom fluid $(y<0)$. Note that the wave vector $k$ (also playing the role of the amplitude decay constant) and the frequency $\omega$ have to be the same for both fluids, because the fluid velocities (and hence displacements) at the interface (at $y=0$ ), calculated from these potentials, should match for all $z$ and $t$ :

$$
\begin{aligned}
& \left.v_{y}\right|_{y=0} \equiv-\left.\frac{\partial \phi_{\mathrm{e}}}{\partial y}\right|_{y=0}=\operatorname{Re}\left[k \Phi_{\mathrm{e}} e^{i(k z-\omega t)}\right]=\operatorname{Re}\left[-k \Phi_{\mathrm{e}} e^{i(k z-\omega t)}\right] \\
& \left.v_{z}\right|_{y=0} \equiv-\left.\frac{\partial \phi_{\mathrm{e}}}{\partial z}\right|_{y=0}=\operatorname{Re}\left[-i k \Phi_{\mathrm{e}} e^{i(k z-\omega t)}\right]=\operatorname{Re}\left[-i k \Phi_{\mathrm{e}} e^{i(k z-\omega t)}\right]
\end{aligned}
$$

The last equalities of each line are evidently compatible if ${ }^{21}$

$$
\Phi_{\mathrm{e}}=-\Phi_{+}^{*}
$$

Another matching condition at the interface is the equality of values $\mathcal{P}_{ \pm}$of pressure in each fluid (valid at negligible surface tension). These values may be calculated from Eq. (8.45), written for each fluid. Integrated over coordinates (within each fluid), it yields

$$
\mathcal{P}_{ \pm}=\rho_{\mathrm{e}}\left(\frac{\partial \phi_{\mathrm{e}}}{\partial t}-g y\right)
$$

(in addition to inconsequential constants). With the substitution of $\phi_{ \pm}$, and the same small-amplitude approximation

$$
y \rightarrow q_{y}=\left.\int v_{y}\right|_{y=0} d t=\operatorname{Re}\left[i \frac{k}{\omega} \Phi_{\mathrm{e}} e^{i(k z-\omega t)}\right]=\operatorname{Re}\left[-i \frac{k}{\omega} \Phi_{\mathrm{e}} e^{i(k z-\omega t)}\right]
$$

[^0]
[^0]:    ${ }^{21}$ Note that because of this equality, the potential amplitudes could not be taken real, as was done in section 8.4 for a single fluid. 
 as was discussed for a single fluid in section 8.4 , the requirement $\mathcal{P}_{+}=\mathcal{P}_{-}$yields the following condition:

$$
\operatorname{Re}\left[\rho_{k}\left(-i \omega \Phi_{k}\right)-\rho_{k} g\left(i \frac{k}{\omega} \Phi_{k}\right)\right]=\operatorname{Re}\left[\rho_{-}\left(-i \omega \Phi_{-}\right)-\rho_{-} g\left(-i \frac{k}{\omega} \Phi_{-}\right)\right]
$$

According to Eq. (*), we may express the potential amplitudes as $\Phi_{+}=a+i b$, $\Phi_{-}=-a+i b$, where $a$ and $b$ are real. Plugging these expressions into Eq. (**), we obtain a homogeneous linear equation,

$$
\rho_{k}\left(\omega+g \frac{k}{\omega}\right) b=\rho_{-}\left(\omega-g \frac{k}{\omega}\right) b
$$

which may give a non-vanishing amplitude $b$ only if

$$
\rho_{k}\left(\omega+g \frac{k}{\omega}\right)=\rho_{-}\left(\omega-g \frac{k}{\omega}\right)
$$

This equation may be readily solved for $\omega^{2}$, giving the dispersion relation,

$$
\omega^{2}=\frac{\rho_{-}-\rho_{k}}{\rho_{-}+\rho_{k}} g k
$$

which is evidently a generalization of Eq. (8.47)-to which Eq. (***) reduces at $\rho_{+} \rightarrow 0$.

According to Eq. (***), as the top fluid becomes heavier, the same $k$ requires a lower $\omega$, i.e. the interface wave becomes slower, and its velocity formally vanishes at $\rho_{+}=\rho_{-}$. This is natural, because if the fluids have the same density, a static deformation of their interface does not carry any energy penalty (provided that we ignore the surface tension-as was done in the above analysis) and may persist forever. However, the most interesting corollary of Eq. $\left({ }^{* * *}\right)$ is that if the top fluid is heavier $\left(\rho_{+}>\rho_{-}\right), \omega^{2}$ becomes negative and $\omega$ becomes purely imaginary. This means that the interface is unstable; indeed, the exponents $\exp \{-i(k z-\omega t)\}$ in our solution become exponential functions of time. This result is also natural, because any attempt to put a layer of a heavier fluid on the top of a lighter one would result is a spontaneous transient process, which would eventually lead to the flipping of these two layers. (Our linear equations may adequately describe only the initial stage of this transient.)

question:
推导一个二维微分方程，描述在一个理想、不可压缩流体的宽广、平面层表面传播的相对长的 $(\lambda \gg h)$ 波，并用它来计算覆盖半径为 $R \gg h$ 的球形行星的层中的最长驻波模式和频率。

提示：最后一项任务需要对球谐函数的基本性质有一定的了解。
solution:
解答：首先让我们考虑一个平面层。然后，通过推广讲义第8.4节中讨论的方法，以及问题8.9的模型解，我们可以寻找以如下形式表示的欧拉方程(8.26)的解：

$$
F_{\omega}(\theta, \varphi+2 \pi)=F_{\omega}(\theta, \varphi)
$$

其中，$\theta$ 和 $\varphi$ 是常用的球坐标（其中 $0 \leqslant \theta \leqslant \pi$）。在这些坐标下，方程$\left({ }^{* * *}\right)$的形式为：

$$
\frac{1}{R^{2}}\left[\frac{1}{\sin \theta} \frac{\partial}{\partial \theta}\left(\sin \theta \frac{\partial}{\partial \theta}\right)+\frac{1}{\sin ^{2} \theta} \frac{\partial^{2}}{\partial \varphi^{2}}\right] F_{\omega}+k^{2} F_{\omega}=0
$$

该方程的本征函数，具有周期性$\left({ }^{* * * *}\right)$，要么是所谓的球谐函数$Y_{l}^{m}(\theta, \varphi)$，要么是它们的实线性组合$Y_{l m}(\theta, \varphi)$，其中$l$和$m$是整数（受限于关系$l \geqslant 0$，且$-l \leqslant m \leqslant+l$）；对应的$k^{2}$的本征值为：

$$
k_{l}^{2}=\frac{l(l+1)}{R^{2}}, \quad \text {因此 } \omega_{l}=v k_{l}=\frac{v}{R}[l(l+1)]^{1 / 2}
$$

（如该公式所示，本征值与$m$无关，即是（$2 l+1$）重的。）

然而，并非该频谱的所有模式都可以用于表面波，因为流体的不可压缩性（即流体体积守恒）对表面位移$\left(q_{y}\right)_{\omega} \propto \operatorname{Re}\left[F_{\omega}\right]$施加了以下附加限制：

$$
\oint_{4 \pi}\left(q_{y}\right)_{\omega} d \Omega \equiv \int_{0}^{\pi} \sin \theta d \theta \int_{0}^{2 \pi} d \varphi\left(q_{y}\right)_{\omega}=0
$$

这一要求禁止了最低模式$l=m=0$（其中$Y_{0}^{0}(\theta, \varphi)=Y_{00}(\theta, \varphi)=$常量），这将对应于流体层的均匀膨胀并具有频率$\omega_{0}=0$；所有其他模式均满足此要求。因此，最低频率的驻波是三个模式$l=1$，$m=-1,0,+1$，其形式可以选择为：

$$
Y_{10}=a \cos \theta, \quad Y_{1(+1)}=a \sin \theta \cos \varphi, \quad Y_{1(-1)}=a \sin \theta \sin \varphi
$$

（由于这些驻波仅因其空间方向不同而不同，并具有相同的频率$\omega_{1}=\sqrt{2} v / R$，它们的任何线性组合也描述了一种可能的驻波。）注意，一个“平面”波（不仅$k=$常量，而且$\mathbf{k}=$常量），其波数对应的值为$k_{1}=\sqrt{2} / R$，将具有波长$\lambda_{1}=2 \pi / k_{1}=\sqrt{2} \pi R \approx 4.44 R$，而不是一个可能天真地猜测的$2 \pi R$，忽略了球体的曲率。

如果这个简单模型应用于地球的海洋，取$R=R_{\mathrm{E}} \approx 6.37 \times 10^{6} \mathrm{~m}$，$g \approx 9.8 \mathrm{~m} \mathrm{~s}^{-2}$，和$h$等于海洋的平均深度$3.7 \times 10^{3} \mathrm{~m}$（从而完全忽略陆地的散射效应），它给出了$v \approx 190 \mathrm{~m} \mathrm{~s}^{-1}$和$\omega_{1} \approx 4.2 \times 10^{-5} \mathrm{~s}^{-1}$，对应的时间周期$\mathscr{T}_{1} \equiv 2 \pi / \omega_{1} \approx 1.5 \times 10^{5} \mathrm{~s} \approx$ 41小时。然而，请注意，由于水的粘性（见下文问题8.18）导致的波的衰减计算表明，即使波没有被大陆和岛屿散射，这种共振的$Q$因子也会相当低。

问题8.12。计算在两种不同密度的理想、不可压缩、不混合流体的水平界面上传播的波的速度分布和色散关系。

解答：由于描述每种流体内部流体动力学的方程（假设位于水平面$y=0$的下方和上方），波结构与单一流体表面上的相同（见讲义第8.4节，特别是图8.7和方程(8.42)），其幅度在每个流体中衰减：

$$
\phi_{\mathrm{e}}=\operatorname{Re}\left[\Phi_{\mathrm{e}} e^{i(k z-\omega t) \tau k y}\right]
$$

其中，上符号指代上方流体（位于$y>0$），下符号指代下方流体（$y<0$）。注意，波矢量$k$（也扮演幅度衰减常数的角色）和频率$\omega$对于两种流体必须相同，因为界面（在$y=0$处）的流体速度（因此位移），计算自这些势能，应该在所有$z$和$t$时匹配：

$$
\begin{aligned}
& \left.v_{y}\right|_{y=0} \equiv-\left.\frac{\partial \phi_{\mathrm{e}}}{\partial y}\right|_{y=0}=\operatorname{Re}\left[k \Phi_{\mathrm{e}} e^{i(k z-\omega t)}\right]=\operatorname{Re}\left[-k \Phi_{\mathrm{e}} e^{i(k z-\omega t)}\right] \\
& \left.v_{z}\right|_{y=0} \equiv-\left.\frac{\partial \phi_{\mathrm{e}}}{\partial z}\right|_{y=0}=\operatorname{Re}\left[-i k \Phi_{\mathrm{e}} e^{i(k z-\omega t)}\right]=\operatorname{Re}\left[-i k \Phi_{\mathrm{e}} e^{i(k z-\omega t)}\right]
\end{aligned}
$$

每行的最后等式显然是兼容的，如果：

$$
\Phi_{\mathrm{e}}=-\Phi_{+}^{*}
$$

界面处的另一个匹配条件是每种流体中的压力值$\mathcal{P}_{ \pm}$的相等（在可忽略的表面张力下有效）。这些值可以从方程(8.45)计算得出，针对每种流体进行书写。积分于坐标（在每种流体内），得到：

$$
\mathcal{P}_{ \pm}=\rho_{\mathrm{e}}\left(\frac{\partial \phi_{\mathrm{e}}}{\partial t}-g y\right)
$$

（除了无关紧要的常数）。通过替换$\phi_{ \pm}$，以及相同的小振幅近似：

$$
y \rightarrow q_{y}=\left.\int v_{y}\right|_{y=0} d t=\operatorname{Re}\left[i \frac{k}{\omega} \Phi_{\mathrm{e}} e^{i(k z-\omega t)}\right]=\operatorname{Re}\left[-i \frac{k}{\omega} \Phi_{\mathrm{e}} e^{i(k z-\omega t)}\right]
$$

如在单一流体中讨论的第8.4节，要求$\mathcal{P}_{+}=\mathcal{P}_{-}$给出了以下条件：

$$
\operatorname{Re}\left[\rho_{k}\left(-i \omega \Phi_{k}\right)-\rho_{k} g\left(i \frac{k}{\omega} \Phi_{k}\right)\right]=\operatorname{Re}\left[\rho_{-}\left(-i \omega \Phi_{-}\right)-\rho_{-} g\left(-i \frac{k}{\omega} \Phi_{-}\right)\right]
$$

根据方程(*)，我们可以将势能幅度表示为$\Phi_{+}=a+i b$，$\Phi_{-}=-a+i b$，其中$a$和$b$是实数。将这些表达式代入方程(**)，我们得到一个齐次线性方程：

$$
\rho_{k}\left(\omega+g \frac{k}{\omega}\right) b=\rho_{-}\left(\omega-g \frac{k}{\omega}\right) b
$$

这可能仅在以下情况下给出一个非零幅度$b$：

$$
\rho_{k}\left(\omega+g \frac{k}{\omega}\right)=\rho_{-}\left(\omega-g \frac{k}{\omega}\right)
$$

这个方程可以很容易地解出$\omega^{2}$，得到色散关系：

$$
\omega^{2}=\frac{\rho_{-}-\rho_{k}}{\rho_{-}+\rho_{k}} g k
$$

这显然是方程(8.47)的一个推广——在$\rho_{+} \rightarrow 0$时，方程(***)会简化为此。

根据方程(***)，当上层流体变重时，相同的$k$需要更低的$\omega$，即界面波变慢，其速度在$\rho_{+}=\rho_{-}$时形式上消失。这是自然的，因为如果流体具有相同的密度，其界面的静态变形不会带来任何能量损失（假设我们忽略了表面张力——如上述分析中所做），并可能永远持续。然而，方程$\left({ }^{* * *}\right)$最有趣的推论是，如果上层流体较重$\left(\rho_{+}>\rho_{-}\right)$，$\omega^{2}$变为负数，$\omega$变为纯虚数。这意味着界面是不稳定的；实际上，我们解中的指数$\exp \{-i(k z-\omega t)\}$变为时间的指数函数。这个结果也是自然的，因为任何试图将较重的流体层放在较轻的流体层之上都会导致一个自发的瞬态过程，最终导致这两个层的翻转。（我们的线性方程只能充分描述这个瞬态的初始阶段。）

question: Derive a general expression for mechanical energy loss rate in a viscous incompressible fluid that obeys the Navier-Stokes equation, and use this expression to calculate the attenuation coefficient of the surface waves, assuming that the viscosity is small. (Quantify this condition).
solution:
Solution: Perhaps the simplest (although not the most rigorous ${ }^{27}$ ) way to calculate the energy loss rate is to use the general Eq. (7.30) for the elementary work of stress forces (per unit volume)
$$\delta \varepsilon \varepsilon^{\prime} \equiv-\sum_{j, j^{\prime}=1}^{3} \sigma_{j j} \delta s_{j^{\prime} j}$$
where, according to Eq. (7.9b), the variation of the symmetric strain tensor $s_{j j^{\prime}}$ may be represented as
$$\delta s_{j j^{\prime}} \equiv \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{\partial\left(\delta q_{j}\right)}{\partial r_{j^{\prime}}}+\frac{\partial\left(\delta q_{j^{\prime}}\right)}{\partial r_{j}}\right)$$
Let us apply these expressions to the variation $\delta s_{j j^{\prime}}$ taking place in a unit volume of a fluid during a small time interval $\delta t$. Plugging in the stress tensor given by Eq. (8.51) into Eq. (*), and dividing both sides by $\delta t$, we obtain
$$\frac{\delta \varepsilon \varepsilon^{\prime}}{\delta t}=\not \partial \frac{1}{\delta t} \sum_{j} \delta \sigma_{j j}-\sum_{j, j^{\prime}=1}^{3} \delta_{j j^{\prime}}(\mathbf{v}) \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{\partial\left(\delta q_{j} / \delta t\right)}{\partial r_{j^{\prime}}}+\frac{\partial\left(\delta q_{j^{\prime}} / \delta t\right)}{\partial r_{j}}\right)$$
But according to Eq. (7.13), the first sum is just $\delta V / V$, while the last operand in the second term describes elements of the tensor e that is defined by Eq. (8.52b),
$$e_{j j^{\prime}}=\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{\partial v_{j}}{\partial r_{j^{\prime}}}+\frac{\partial v_{j^{\prime}}}{\partial r_{j}}\right)$$
so that we may write
$$\frac{\delta \varepsilon \varepsilon^{\prime}}{\delta t}=\frac{\not \partial \delta V}{V \delta t}+\frac{\delta \varepsilon}{\delta t}, \quad \text { where } \frac{\delta \varepsilon}{\delta t} \equiv-\sum_{j, j^{\prime}=1}^{3} \delta_{j j} e_{j^{\prime} j}$$
The first term evidently describes the reversible change of the bulk compression energy of the fluid, while the second term, which depends only on the fluid velocity distribution (and is constant in time if $\mathbf{v}=\mathbf{v}(\mathbf{r})$ only), represents the rate of irreversible energy loss (per unit volume).
For an incompressible fluid, $\operatorname{Tr}(\mathrm{e})=0$, so that Eq. (8.52), describing the viscosity effects in the Navier-Stokes approximation, is reduced to
$$\delta_{j j}(\mathbf{v})=2 \eta e_{j j}$$
and the above expression for energy loss may be rewritten as
$$\frac{\delta e}{\delta t}=-2 \eta \sum_{j, j^{\prime}=1}^{3} e_{j j^{\prime}}^{2}$$
Now moving to the second task, as it follows from the discussion in section 6.6 of the lecture notes, the wave attenuation along the direction (say, $z$) of its propagation may be characterized by coefficient
$$\alpha \equiv-\frac{d E / d z}{E}$$
where $E$ is the local energy of a wave with a time-independent spatial distribution ${ }^{28}$. If the attenuation is so weak that $\alpha$ is much smaller than the wave number $k$ (i.e. if the wavelength $\lambda=2 \pi / k$ is much smaller than the decay length $l_{d}=1 / \alpha$ ), we may calculate the energy dissipation rate ignoring the viscosity effect on the local $\left(\Delta z \sim \lambda \ll l_{d}\right)$ distribution of the fluid velocity components. For the surface waves analyzed in section 8.4 of the lecture notes, these distributions are given by Eq. (8.43), and since in that 'plane' wave $\partial / \partial x=0$, the only non-vanishing elements of the tensor e are,
$$\begin{gathered}
e_{22}=\frac{\partial v_{y}}{\partial y}=k^{2} \Phi_{4} e^{k y} \cos (k z-\omega t), \quad e_{33}=\frac{\partial v_{z}}{\partial z}=-k^{2} \Phi_{4} e^{k y} \cos (k z-\omega t) \
e_{23}=e_{32}=\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{\partial v_{y}}{\partial z}+\frac{\partial v_{z}}{\partial y}\right)=k^{2} \Phi_{4} e^{k y} \sin (k z-\omega t)\end{gathered}$$
so that in this case the energy loss rate $\left(^{*}\right)$ does not depend on $z$ and $t$ :
$$\frac{\delta e}{\delta t}=-2 \eta \sum_{j, j^{\prime}=1}^{3} e_{j j^{\prime}}^{2}=-4 \eta k^{4} \Phi_{A}^{2} e^{2 k y}$$

question: 推导一个服从Navier-Stokes方程的粘性不可压缩流体的机械能损失率的一般表达式，并使用该表达式计算表面波的衰减系数，假设粘度很小。（量化此条件）。
solution:
解答：或许最简单（尽管不是最严格的${ }^{27}$）计算能量损失率的方法是使用广义方程(7.30)，用于应力力的基本功（每单位体积）的计算
$$\delta \varepsilon \varepsilon^{\prime} \equiv-\sum_{j, j^{\prime}=1}^{3} \sigma_{j j} \delta s_{j^{\prime} j}$$
根据方程(7.9b)，对称应变张量$s_{j j^{\prime}}$的变化可以表示为
$$\delta s_{j j^{\prime}} \equiv \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{\partial\left(\delta q_{j}\right)}{\partial r_{j^{\prime}}}+\frac{\partial\left(\delta q_{j^{\prime}}\right)}{\partial r_{j}}\right)$$
让我们将这些表达式应用于单位体积流体在小时间间隔$\delta t$内发生的变化$\delta s_{j j^{\prime}}$。将方程(8.51)给出的应力张量代入方程(*)，并将两边除以$\delta t$，我们得到
$$\frac{\delta \varepsilon \varepsilon^{\prime}}{\delta t}=\not \partial \frac{1}{\delta t} \sum_{j} \delta \sigma_{j j}-\sum_{j, j^{\prime}=1}^{3} \delta_{j j^{\prime}}(\mathbf{v}) \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{\partial\left(\delta q_{j} / \delta t\right)}{\partial r_{j^{\prime}}}+\frac{\partial\left(\delta q_{j^{\prime}} / \delta t\right)}{\partial r_{j}}\right)$$
但根据方程(7.13)，第一个求和只是$\delta V / V$，而第二项中的最后一个操作数描述了由方程(8.52b)定义的张量e的元素，
$$e_{j j^{\prime}}=\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{\partial v_{j}}{\partial r_{j^{\prime}}}+\frac{\partial v_{j^{\prime}}}{\partial r_{j}}\right)$$
因此我们可以写为
$$\frac{\delta \varepsilon \varepsilon^{\prime}}{\delta t}=\frac{\not \partial \delta V}{V \delta t}+\frac{\delta \varepsilon}{\delta t}, \quad \text { 其中 } \frac{\delta \varepsilon}{\delta t} \equiv-\sum_{j, j^{\prime}=1}^{3} \delta_{j j} e_{j^{\prime} j}$$
显然，第一项描述了流体体积压缩能量的可逆变化，而第二项仅依赖于流体速度分布（如果$\mathbf{v}=\mathbf{v}(\mathbf{r})$仅为此时为常数），代表不可逆能量损失率（每单位体积）。
对于不可压缩流体，$\operatorname{Tr}(\mathrm{e})=0$，因此描述Navier-Stokes近似中粘性效应的方程(8.52)简化为
$$\delta_{j j}(\mathbf{v})=2 \eta e_{j j}$$
上述能量损失的表达式可以重写为
$$\frac{\delta e}{\delta t}=-2 \eta \sum_{j, j^{\prime}=1}^{3} e_{j j^{\prime}}^{2}$$
现在转到第二个任务，正如讲义第6.6节中的讨论所示，沿其传播方向（例如$z$）的波衰减可以通过系数表征
$$\alpha \equiv-\frac{d E / d z}{E}$$
其中$E$是具有时间不变空间分布的波的局部能量${ }^{28}$。如果衰减非常弱以至于$\alpha$远小于波数$k$（即如果波长$\lambda=2 \pi / k$远小于衰减长度$l_{d}=1 / \alpha$），我们可以忽略对流体速度分量局部$\left(\Delta z \sim \lambda \ll l_{d}\right)$分布的粘性影响来计算能量消散率。对于讲义第8.4节中分析的表面波，这些分布由方程(8.43)给出，由于在该“平面”波中$\partial / \partial x=0$，张量e的唯一非零元素为，
$$\begin{gathered}
e_{22}=\frac{\partial v_{y}}{\partial y}=k^{2} \Phi_{4} e^{k y} \cos (k z-\omega t), \quad e_{33}=\frac{\partial v_{z}}{\partial z}=-k^{2} \Phi_{4} e^{k y} \cos (k z-\omega t) \
e_{23}=e_{32}=\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{\partial v_{y}}{\partial z}+\frac{\partial v_{z}}{\partial y}\right)=k^{2} \Phi_{4} e^{k y} \sin (k z-\omega t)\end{gathered}$$
因此在这种情况下能量损失率$\left(^{*}\right)$不依赖于$z$和$t$：
$$\frac{\delta e}{\delta t}=-2 \eta \sum_{j, j^{\prime}=1}^{3} e_{j j^{\prime}}^{2}=-4 \eta k^{4} \Phi_{A}^{2} e^{2 k y}$$。

question: What is the expression for the intensity $I(x)$ in a Young two-slit interference experiment, and how is the interfringe distance $x_0$ related to the wavelength $\lambda$, the slit distance $a$, and the screen distance $D$?
solution: The amplitude at point $C$ is the sum of the amplitudes from the two slits: $A_C = A_1 + A_2$. The intensity $I(x)$ at a point on the screen is given by the modulus squared of the amplitude: $I(x) = |A_C|^2$. The intensity presents a periodic variation in $x$, with the interfringe distance $x_0$ given by $x_0 = \frac{\lambda D}{a}$, where $\lambda$ is the wavelength, $D$ is the distance to the screen, and $a$ is the distance between the slits.

question: 在杨氏双缝干涉实验中，强度 $I(x)$ 的表达式是什么，且条纹间距 $x_0$ 与波长 $\lambda$、缝距 $a$ 和屏幕距离 $D$ 之间有何关系？
solution: 点$C$处的振幅是来自两个狭缝的振幅之和：$A_C = A_1 + A_2$。屏幕上某点的强度$I(x)$由振幅的模平方给出：$I(x) = |A_C|^2$。强度在$x$上呈现周期性变化，条纹间距$x_0$由以下公式给出：$x_0 = \frac{\lambda D}{a}$，其中$\lambda$是波长，$D$是到屏幕的距离，$a$是狭缝之间的距离。

question:
Consider a one-dimensional system of Hamiltonian $\hat{H}=\hat{p}^{2} / 2 m+V(\hat{x})$ where $V(x)=\lambda x^{n}$.
 a. Calculate the commutator $[\hat{H}, \hat{x} \hat{p}]$.
 b. By taking the expectation value of this commutator, show that in any eigenstate of $\hat{H}$, one has the relation:
 $$
 2\langle T\rangle=n\langle V\rangle
 $$
 where $\hat{T}=\hat{p}^{2} / 2 m$ is the kinetic energy operator. Check this relation on the harmonic oscillator.
 c. Generalize this result to three dimensions by calculating $[\hat{H}, \hat{\boldsymbol{r}} \cdot \hat{\boldsymbol{p}}]$ and considering a potential $V(\boldsymbol{r})$ which is a homogeneous function of the variables $x, y, z$, of degree $n$. A homogeneous function of degree $n$ satisfies $V(\alpha x, \alpha y, \alpha z)=$ $\alpha^{n} V(x, y, z)$ and $\boldsymbol{r} \cdot \nabla V=n V$.
 d. Show that for an arbitrary potential $V(r)$ one has the general relation:
 $$
 2\langle T\rangle=\left\langle r \frac{\partial V}{\partial r}\right\rangle
 $$
solution:
a. The commutator $[\hat{H}, \hat{x} \hat{p}]$ can be calculated using the commutator identities and properties of operators. The commutator $[\hat{H}, \hat{x} \hat{p}] = [\hat{p}^2/2m, \hat{x}\hat{p}] + [V(\hat{x}), \hat{x}\hat{p}]$ simplifies to $i\hbar \hat{p}/m + i\hbar n V(\hat{x})$.

b. Taking the expectation value of the commutator from part (a), we have $\langle [\hat{H}, \hat{x} \hat{p}] \rangle = 0$ for any eigenstate of $\hat{H}$. This leads to the relation $2\langle T \rangle = n\langle V \rangle$. For the harmonic oscillator, where $V(x) = \frac{1}{2}m\omega^2x^2$, the relation holds since $n=2$ and $2\langle T \rangle = 2\langle V \rangle$.

c. In three dimensions, the commutator $[\hat{H}, \hat{\boldsymbol{r}} \cdot \hat{\boldsymbol{p}}]$ can be calculated similarly, resulting in $i\hbar \hat{\boldsymbol{p}}^2/m + i\hbar n V(\hat{\boldsymbol{r}})$. The relation generalizes to $2\langle T \rangle = n\langle V \rangle$ for a homogeneous potential of degree $n$.

 d. For an arbitrary potential $V(r)$, using the radial derivative, the general relation $2\langle T \rangle = \left\langle r \frac{\partial V}{\partial r} \right\rangle$ is derived from the expectation value of the commutator $\langle [\hat{H}, \hat{x} \hat{p}] \rangle = 0$.

question:
考虑一个一维系统，其哈密顿量为 $\hat{H}=\hat{p}^{2} / 2 m+V(\hat{x})$，其中 $V(x)=\lambda x^{n}$。
a. 计算对易子 $[\hat{H}, \hat{x} \hat{p}]$。
b. 通过取该对易子的期望值，证明在 $\hat{H}$ 的任一本征态中，有如下关系：
$$
2\langle T\rangle=n\langle V\rangle
$$
其中 $\hat{T}=\hat{p}^{2} / 2 m$ 是动能算符。检验这一关系在谐振子中的成立。
c. 通过计算 $[\hat{H}, \hat{\boldsymbol{r}} \cdot \hat{\boldsymbol{p}}]$ 并考虑一个势能 $V(\boldsymbol{r})$ 是变量 $x, y, z$ 的齐次函数，阶数为 $n$，将这一结果推广到三维。阶数为 $n$ 的齐次函数满足 $V(\alpha x, \alpha y, \alpha z)=\alpha^{n} V(x, y, z)$ 且 $\boldsymbol{r} \cdot \nabla V=n V$。
d. 证明对于任意势能 $V(r)$，有如下通用关系：
$$
2\langle T\rangle=\left\langle r \frac{\partial V}{\partial r}\right\rangle
$$。
solution:
a. 计算对易子 $[\hat{H}, \hat{x} \hat{p}]$ 可以使用对易子恒等式和算符的性质。对易子 $[\hat{H}, \hat{x} \hat{p}] = [\hat{p}^2/2m, \hat{x}\hat{p}] + [V(\hat{x}), \hat{x}\hat{p}]$ 简化为 $i\hbar \hat{p}/m + i\hbar n V(\hat{x})$。

b. 对于部分 (a) 的对易子取期望值，我们有 $\langle [\hat{H}, \hat{x} \hat{p}] \rangle = 0$，对于任何 $\hat{H}$ 的本征态。这导致关系 $2\langle T \rangle = n\langle V \rangle$。对于谐振子，其中 $V(x) = \frac{1}{2}m\omega^2x^2$，该关系成立，因为 $n=2$ 且 $2\langle T \rangle = 2\langle V \rangle$。

c. 在三维中，对易子 $[\hat{H}, \hat{\boldsymbol{r}} \cdot \hat{\boldsymbol{p}}]$ 可以类似地计算，结果为 $i\hbar \hat{\boldsymbol{p}}^2/m + i\hbar n V(\hat{\boldsymbol{r}})$。对于次数为 $n$ 的齐次势，关系推广为 $2\langle T \rangle = n\langle V \rangle$。

d. 对于任意势 $V(r)$，使用径向导数，从对易子的期望值 $\langle [\hat{H}, \hat{x} \hat{p}] \rangle = 0$ 推导出一般关系 $2\langle T \rangle = \left\langle r \frac{\partial V}{\partial r} \right\rangle$。

question: Consider two angular momentum observables $\hat{\boldsymbol{j}}_{1}$ and $\hat{\boldsymbol{j}}_{2}$. In the subspace corresponding to given values $j_{1}$ and $j_{2}$, what are the possible values for the quantum number $j$ associated with the total angular momentum $\hat{\boldsymbol{j}}$, assuming that $j_{1} \geq j_{2}$?
solution:
The possible values for the quantum number $j$ associated with the total angular momentum $\hat{\boldsymbol{j}}$ are given by:

$$
j \in\left\{j_{1}+j_{2}, j_{1}+j_{2}-1, j_{1}+j_{2}-2, \ldots, j_{1}-j_{2}+1, j_{1}-j_{2}\right\}
$$

question: 考虑两个角动量可观测量 $\hat{\boldsymbol{j}}_{1}$ 和 $\hat{\boldsymbol{j}}_{2}$。在对应于给定值 $j_{1}$ 和 $j_{2}$ 的子空间中，与总角动量 $\hat{\boldsymbol{j}}$ 相关的量子数 $j$ 的可能取值是什么，假设 $j_{1} \geq j_{2}$？
solution:
与总角动量 $\hat{\boldsymbol{j}}$ 相关的量子数 $j$ 的可能取值为：

$$
j \in\left\{j_{1}+j_{2}, j_{1}+j_{2}-1, j_{1}+j_{2}-2, \ldots, j_{1}-j_{2}+1, j_{1}-j_{2}\right\}
$$。

solution:
a. One must have $\int_{0}^{\infty}|R(r)|^{2} r^{2} d r=1 / 2$ since the $Y_{\ell}^{m}$ 's are orthonormal and $\int\left(\left|\psi_{+}\right|^{2}+\left|\psi_{-}\right|^{2}\right) d^{3} r=1$

solution:
